Old Helm stopped at a stone stall and smiled. 'This is the *traditional* way we enter every new island,' he said, pressing a small coin into the seller's hand. 'It opens doors.'
traditional:1.cnHint: 老舵主告诉我，在每座新岛上，按____的方式拜访市集，是打开人心的钥匙。
traditional:1.hook: But the coin began to glow, and the seller's eyes went wide.
traditional:1.line: 'This is the *traditional* way we enter every new island,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: The storm island market was nothing like I expected.
sentences.cn: 风暴岛的市集不像我想象的那样。

sentences.en: Vendors called out from beneath bright cloth roofs, and the air smelled of warm bread and spice.
sentences.cn: 小商贩在明亮的布棚下叫卖，空气里弥漫着热面包和香料的味道。

sentences.en: Old Helm stopped at a stone stall and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵在一个石制摊位停了下来，微笑着。

sentences.en: 'This is the *traditional* way we enter every new island,' he said, pressing a small coin into the seller's hand.
'It opens doors.'
sentences.cn: '这就是进入每一个新岛屿的传统方式，'他说，把一枚小硬币塞进卖家的手里。

expert:1.en: The rope bridge over the storm gap was frayed and swaying hard. Bell studied each knot without touching anything, her eyes calm and steady. She was a clear *expert* in the art of reading worn rope — every twist told her whether it would hold or snap. 'Third knot from the left,' she said at last. 'Replace it and we cross safely.'
expert:1.cnHint: 小铃是绳桥的____，只用眼睛就能判断哪根绳子危险。
expert:1.hook: Then the wind doubled, and the whole bridge lurched sideways.
expert:1.line: 'I am the *expert* here — trust the third knot,' said Bell.

sentences.en: The rope bridge over the storm gap was frayed and swaying hard.
sentences.cn: 跨越风暴间隙的绳桥散开着，在风中摇晃得厉害。

sentences.en: Bell studied each knot without touching anything, her eyes calm and steady.
sentences.cn: 小铃仔细研究每一个结，眼睛平静而沉着。

sentences.en: She was a clear *expert* in the art of reading worn rope — every twist told her whether it would hold or snap.
'Third knot from the left,' she said at last.
sentences.cn: '从左数第三个结，'她最后说道。

sentences.en: 'Replace it and we cross safely.'
sentences.cn: '换掉它，我们就能安全通过。'

member:1.en: We gathered on the open deck as the storm clouds rolled in. Old Helm looked at each face slowly. 'Every *member* of this troupe carries a piece of the map,' he said. 'Lose one person and we lose one path.' The stars above us flickered, as if agreeing. I felt, for the first time, that I truly belonged here.
member:1.cnHint: 老舵主提醒大家，每位____都是地图的一部分，缺一不可。
member:1.hook: Then Silverfang pointed to an empty spot on the deck.
member:1.line: 'Every *member* of this troupe carries a piece of the map,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: We gathered on the open deck as the storm clouds rolled in.
sentences.cn: 我们聚集在敞开的甲板上，风暴云卷了进来。

sentences.en: Old Helm looked at each face slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵慢慢地看着每一张脸。

sentences.en: 'Every *member* of this troupe carries a piece of the map,' he said.
'Lose one person and we lose one path.'
sentences.cn: '这个团队的每一个成员都掌握着地图的一部分，'他说。

sentences.en: The stars above us flickered, as if agreeing.
sentences.cn: 失去一个人，我们就失去一条路。

sentences.en: I felt, for the first time, that I truly belonged here.
sentences.cn: 头顶的星光闪烁，仿佛在赞同。

heart:1.en: Silverfang spread the storm chart across the barrel and tapped its centre hard. 'This mark,' she said, 'is the *heart* of the storm zone — the one place where the wind goes completely still.' Bell raised an eyebrow. I leaned closer. If the wind truly died there, we could release a new word-fragment without it blowing away into the dark sky.
heart:1.cnHint: 银牙在海图上指出风暴区的____，那里据说风会完全静止。
heart:1.hook: But the chart showed the heart was already moving toward us.
heart:1.line: 'This mark is the *heart* of the storm zone,' said Silverfang.

sentences.en: Silverfang spread the storm chart across the barrel and tapped its centre hard.
sentences.cn: 银牙把风暴图铺在桶上，用力敲了敲中心。

sentences.en: 'This mark,' she said, 'is the *heart* of the storm zone — the one place where the wind goes completely still.'
Bell raised an eyebrow.
sentences.cn: 小铃扬起眉毛。

sentences.en: I leaned closer.
sentences.cn: 我凑得更近了。

sentences.en: If the wind truly died there, we could release a new word-fragment without it blowing away into the dark sky.
sentences.cn: 如果风在那里真的停止了，我们就能释放一个新的词语碎片，而不用担心它被吹向黑暗的天空。

within:1.en: The storm rolled in fast. Old Helm spread a worn chart across the deck and traced a thin safe path *within* the ring of black clouds. Bell leaned close, counting the gaps between lightning strikes. The air smelled of salt and iron, and every second felt borrowed.
within:1.cnHint: 老舵手在甲板上展开海图，指出只要保持在____云圈的范围内就能安全通过。
within:1.hook: The gap in the clouds was closing faster than any of us expected.
within:1.line: 'Stay *within* that ring and the wind will carry us through,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: The storm rolled in fast.
sentences.cn: 风暴来得很急。

sentences.en: Old Helm spread a worn chart across the deck and traced a thin safe path *within* the ring of black clouds.
Bell leaned close, counting the gaps between lightning strikes.
sentences.cn: 小铃靠近身子，数着闪电之间的间隙。

sentences.en: The air smelled of salt and iron, and every second felt borrowed.
sentences.cn: 空气里弥漫着盐和铁的味道，每一秒都像是借来的。

either:1.en: Bell stood at the bow, studying two bridges that arched over the storm-grey channel. One shook in the wind; the other was half swallowed by dark fog. She turned to us and shook her head slowly. *Either* path held danger, yet standing still was not an option the sky would allow.
either:1.cnHint: 领航员发现两座桥都有危险，____一条路都不好走，但船必须前进。
either:1.hook: Then a third shape rose from the water between the bridges.
either:1.line: 'I would not trust *either* bridge on a calm day, let alone tonight,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Bell stood at the bow, studying two bridges that arched over the storm-grey channel.
sentences.cn: 小铃站在船头，研究着两座跨越风暴灰色水道的桥。

sentences.en: One shook in the wind; the other was half swallowed by dark fog.
sentences.cn: 一座在风中摇晃；另一座半没在黑色的雾里。

sentences.en: She turned to us and shook her head slowly.
sentences.cn: 她转向我们，缓缓摇头。

sentences.en: *Either* path held danger, yet standing still was not an option the sky would allow.

various:1.en: Old Helm opened his word-sack and laid out the map fragments on the deck. They came in *various* shapes — triangles, circles, long strips — and each one glowed a different colour when the lightning flashed. Bell began sorting them by brightness while the wind pulled at the edges of every piece.
various:1.cnHint: 老舵手把各种形状的碎片地图铺在甲板上，团队试图在风暴中将它们拼合。
various:1.hook: One fragment spun into the air and sailed straight toward the storm.
various:1.line: 'We have collected *various* pieces, but the centre piece is still missing,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Old Helm opened his word-sack and laid out the map fragments on the deck.
sentences.cn: 老舵打开他的词语袋，把地图碎片铺在甲板上。

sentences.en: They came in *various* shapes — triangles, circles, long strips — and each one glowed a different colour when the lightning flashed.
Bell began sorting them by brightness while the wind pulled at the edges of every piece.
sentences.cn: 小铃开始按亮度给它们分类，风拉扯着每一块的边缘。

main:1.en: The *main* mast groaned as a wave lifted the deck sideways. Bell grabbed the rope and held on, her feet sliding across wet wood. Old Helm pointed up at the single lantern swinging at the top. That small flame, he said, was the only light Silverfang's crew could follow through the black water.
main:1.cnHint: 在风浪中，船的____桅杆发出警报般的呻吟声，那盏灯是友船唯一的引路光。
main:1.hook: The lantern swung hard and then went completely dark.
main:1.line: 'Keep the *main* mast steady or Silverfang will never find us,' Old Helm called out.

sentences.en: The *main* mast groaned as a wave lifted the deck sideways.
Bell grabbed the rope and held on, her feet sliding across wet wood.
sentences.cn: 小铃抓住绳子，紧紧握住，脚在湿木头上滑动。

sentences.en: Old Helm pointed up at the single lantern swinging at the top.
sentences.cn: 老舵指向顶部唯一摇晃的灯笼。

sentences.en: That small flame, he said, was the only light Silverfang's crew could follow through the black water.
sentences.cn: 他说，那盏小火焰是银牙的船员在黑水中唯一能跟随的光。

employee:1.en: A small boat bumped against our hull in the dark. A young woman climbed aboard, soaking wet and breathing hard. She said she had been an *employee* of the sky-chart guild until the storm scattered her whole team across three islands. She carried half a word-fragment wrapped tight against her chest.
employee:1.cnHint: 一个曾是天图公会____的年轻女子爬上了船，她随身带着一块碎片地图。
employee:1.hook: She looked at Old Helm's sack and whispered, 'I know where the rest are.'
employee:1.line: 'I was a loyal *employee* of the guild before the storm broke everything apart,' she said.

sentences.en: A small boat bumped against our hull in the dark.
sentences.cn: 黑暗中，一艘小船撞上了我们的船体。

sentences.en: A young woman climbed aboard, soaking wet and breathing hard.
sentences.cn: 一个年轻女人爬上了甲板，浑身湿透，喘着粗气。

sentences.en: She said she had been an *employee* of the sky-chart guild until the storm scattered her whole team across three islands.
She carried half a word-fragment wrapped tight against her chest.
sentences.cn: 她紧紧抱着半段字符碎片贴在胸口。

class:1.en: Old Helm called everyone to the centre of the deck. 'This storm is a different *class* of danger,' he said, voice steady against the wind. It was not like the soft squalls that tested new crew — this one shifted direction every few minutes, as if it were thinking, as if it chose its targets carefully.
class:1.cnHint: 老舵手告诉大家，这场风暴是完全不同____的危险，远超以往所有经历。
class:1.hook: The storm turned sharply toward us as if it had heard its name.
class:1.line: 'No ordinary squall — this is a *class* of storm I have only read about,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Old Helm called everyone to the centre of the deck.
sentences.cn: 老舵召集所有人到甲板中央。

sentences.en: 'This storm is a different *class* of danger,' he said, voice steady against the wind.
It was not like the soft squalls that tested new crew — this one shifted direction every few minutes, as if it were thinking, as if it chose its targets carefully.
sentences.cn: 这不像考验新手的温和风暴——这一阵每隔几分钟就变向，仿佛在思考，仿佛在精心选择它的目标。

behavior:1.en: Silverfang brought her ship alongside ours, and her navigator handed Bell a small notebook. It was full of observations — hours and hours of recorded *behavior* of the storm: how it paused, how it spun, when it pulled back before striking. Bell's eyes went wide reading the tiny careful handwriting.
behavior:1.cnHint: 竞争船长派人送来一本记录风暴____规律的小册子，领航员读后大为震惊。
behavior:1.hook: The last entry in the notebook simply read: 'It knows we are watching.'
behavior:1.line: 'Study the storm's *behavior* carefully and you will find its one weak moment,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: Silverfang brought her ship alongside ours, and her navigator handed Bell a small notebook.
sentences.cn: 银牙把她的船靠到我们身边，她的航海员递给小铃一本小笔记本。

sentences.en: It was full of observations — hours and hours of recorded *behavior* of the storm: how it paused, how it spun, when it pulled back before striking.
Bell's eyes went wide reading the tiny careful handwriting.
sentences.cn: 小铃读着那工整的细小笔迹，眼睛睁得很大。

disease:1.en: One of the word-fragments on the deck had turned grey and soft, edges crumbling like dry bread. Bell said it looked like a *disease* was spreading through it, eating the map from inside. If it reached the centre glyph, the path to the next island would be lost forever. We had very little time.
disease:1.cnHint: 一块碎片地图开始腐烂，领航员说像是某种____正在从内部侵蚀它。
disease:1.hook: A second fragment began to darken at the corner as we watched.
disease:1.line: 'This *disease* will take the whole chart if we do not find a cure before dawn,' Bell said.

sentences.en: One of the word-fragments on the deck had turned grey and soft, edges crumbling like dry bread.
sentences.cn: 甲板上的一块字符碎片变成了灰色和软绵绵的，边缘像干面包一样碎裂。

sentences.en: Bell said it looked like a *disease* was spreading through it, eating the map from inside.
If it reached the centre glyph, the path to the next island would be lost forever.
sentences.cn: 如果它蔓延到中心纹符，通往下一个岛屿的路径就会永远消失。

sentences.en: We had very little time.
sentences.cn: 我们时间很紧了。

compare:2.en: Bell spread two charts across the storm-shelter table. One showed the old sky-road, drawn by hand long ago. The other was fresh, printed just this morning. 'You can *compare* them side by side,' she said. The difference made my breath stop — a whole island had moved.
compare:2.cnHint: 小铃将两张海图摆在一起，让我们____它们的不同。
compare:2.hook: The shifted island meant someone had changed the sky on purpose.
compare:2.line: '*Compare* the old route with the new one — tell me what you see.'

sentences.en: Bell spread two charts across the storm-shelter table.
sentences.cn: 小铃在防风舱的桌子上展开了两张海图。

sentences.en: One showed the old sky-road, drawn by hand long ago.
sentences.cn: 一张是很久以前手绘的古天路。

sentences.en: The other was fresh, printed just this morning.
sentences.cn: 另一张是新的，今天早上才印的。

sentences.en: 'You can *compare* them side by side,' she said.
The difference made my breath stop — a whole island had moved.
sentences.cn: 差异让我屏住了呼吸——整座岛屿移动了。

past:2.en: Old Helm found a locked chest half buried under the navigation deck. Inside lay letters yellowed with age, maps folded until they cracked, and a name none of us knew. 'The *past* never stays buried on these islands,' he said softly, pressing one letter to the lantern light.
past:2.cnHint: 老舵手打开一只旧箱子，里面藏满了____的秘密。
past:2.hook: The unknown name appeared again — on the newest map.

sentences.en: Old Helm found a locked chest half buried under the navigation deck.
sentences.cn: 老舵在导航甲板下找到了一个半埋的上锁箱子。

sentences.en: Inside lay letters yellowed with age, maps folded until they cracked, and a name none of us knew.
sentences.cn: 里面放着泛黄的信件、折到开裂的地图，还有我们都不认识的一个名字。

sentences.en: 'The *past* never stays buried on these islands,' he said softly, pressing one letter to the lantern light.

suffer:2.en: The storm hit the outer ring of islands just before dawn. Bell held the wheel steady for three hours without rest, her arms shaking. 'I can *suffer* a little tiredness,' she said through her teeth. When the clouds finally broke, we saw the island we had been searching for, right ahead.
suffer:2.cnHint: 小铃在风暴中苦撑，说自己能____这点辛苦。
suffer:2.hook: But the island ahead showed no lights — none at all.

sentences.en: The storm hit the outer ring of islands just before dawn.
sentences.cn: 风暴在黎明前击中了外围岛屿。

sentences.en: Bell held the wheel steady for three hours without rest, her arms shaking.
sentences.cn: 小铃握着舵轮坚守了三个小时没有休息，胳膊在发抖。

sentences.en: 'I can *suffer* a little tiredness,' she said through her teeth.
When the clouds finally broke, we saw the island we had been searching for, right ahead.
sentences.cn: 乌云终于散开时，我们看到了一直在寻找的岛屿，就在前方。

almost:2.en: I reached for the glass bottle caught between two ropes. It held a rolled note inside, sealed with blue wax. My fingers brushed it once, twice — I *almost* dropped it into the open sky below the deck before Bell caught my wrist with a steady hand and smiled.
almost:2.cnHint: 我在绳索间发现了一个玻璃瓶，却____将它失手落下。
almost:2.hook: The note inside bore Old Helm's own signature — dated tomorrow.

sentences.en: I reached for the glass bottle caught between two ropes.
sentences.cn: 我伸手去拿卡在两根绳子之间的玻璃瓶。

sentences.en: It held a rolled note inside, sealed with blue wax.
sentences.cn: 里面装着一张卷起的纸条，用蓝色蜡封着。

sentences.en: My fingers brushed it once, twice — I *almost* dropped it into the open sky below the deck before Bell caught my wrist with a steady hand and smiled.

especially:2.en: Old Helm kept every word-fragment in a small wooden box, *especially* the ones found near storm zones, which he said carried the strongest memories. I opened the box while he slept and found one fragment glowing faintly blue. It pulsed like a heartbeat, slow and even, in my palm.
especially:2.cnHint: 老舵手____珍视暴风区附近找到的词语碎片。
especially:2.hook: The blue glow matched the colour of Silverfang's ship exactly.

sentences.en: Old Helm kept every word-fragment in a small wooden box, *especially* the ones found near storm zones, which he said carried the strongest memories.
I opened the box while he slept and found one fragment glowing faintly blue.
sentences.cn: 他睡着时我打开了盒子，发现一块碎片发出淡淡的蓝光。

sentences.en: It pulsed like a heartbeat, slow and even, in my palm.
sentences.cn: 它在我掌心里搏动，节奏缓慢而均匀，像心跳。

publish:2.en: Silverfang slid a thin book across the table without a word. The cover read: 'Storm-Roads of the Upper Sky.' 'My crew *published* this last season,' she said. 'It shows every safe path through the wind belt.' Old Helm turned the pages slowly, then stopped at a route none of us had ever tried.
publish:2.cnHint: 银牙船长把她船员____的一本航路手册推到了桌上。
publish:2.hook: The route passed directly through the island no one returns from.

sentences.en: Silverfang slid a thin book across the table without a word.
sentences.cn: 银牙默默地把一本薄书推过桌子。

sentences.en: The cover read: 'Storm-Roads of the Upper Sky.'
sentences.cn: 封面写着《上层天空的风暴之路》。

sentences.en: 'My crew *published* this last season,' she said.
'It shows every safe path through the wind belt.'
sentences.cn: "我们的船队上一季出版了这个，"她说。

sentences.en: Old Helm turned the pages slowly, then stopped at a route none of us had ever tried.
sentences.cn: 老舵慢慢翻过几页，然后停在了一条我们谁都没试过的路线。

activity:2.en: Bell pressed her ear to the hull of the old signal tower on the edge of the island. 'There is *activity* inside,' she whispered. 'Something is tapping — a pattern.' We counted the beats together: three short, two long, one short. It was the old sky-code, the one used a hundred years ago.
activity:2.cnHint: 小铃听到信号塔内有____，那是古老的天空电码。
activity:2.hook: The code spelled out a single word: run.

sentences.en: Bell pressed her ear to the hull of the old signal tower on the edge of the island.
sentences.cn: 小铃把耳朵贴在岛边老信号塔的船体上。

sentences.en: 'There is *activity* inside,' she whispered.
'Something is tapping — a pattern.'
sentences.cn: "有什么东西在敲——有规律。"

sentences.en: We counted the beats together: three short, two long, one short.
sentences.cn: 我们一起数着节拍：三短、两长、一短。

sentences.en: It was the old sky-code, the one used a hundred years ago.
sentences.cn: 这是古老的天空密码，一百年前用过的那种。

science:2.en: The fragment we found was shaped like a gear and covered in tiny writing. Old Helm held it close to the lamp. 'This is the language of *science*,' he said with quiet excitement. 'Someone used it to record the storm's own voice.' The writing moved, rearranging itself slowly as we watched.
science:2.cnHint: 老舵手发现这块碎片上记录的是____语言写成的暴风数据。
science:2.hook: The storm's recorded voice began, very softly, to speak.

sentences.en: The fragment we found was shaped like a gear and covered in tiny writing.
sentences.cn: 我们找到的碎片形状像齿轮，上面满是细小的文字。

sentences.en: Old Helm held it close to the lamp.
sentences.cn: 老舵把它靠近灯。

sentences.en: 'This is the language of *science*,' he said with quiet excitement.
'Someone used it to record the storm's own voice.'
sentences.cn: "有人用它记录了风暴自己的声音。"

sentences.en: The writing moved, rearranging itself slowly as we watched.
sentences.cn: 我们看着，文字缓缓重新排列自己。

worker:1.en: The storm island's dock smelled of iron and rain. A lone *worker* was patching ropes by lantern light, hands moving without pause. 'New crew?' he asked without looking up. Old Helm nodded. The man pointed to a gap in the clouds. 'That's where the word hides,' he said. 'Past the white squall.'
worker:1.cnHint: 码头上，一位____在灯光下修补绳索，他指引我们找到隐藏的词语碎片。
worker:1.hook: The gap in the clouds was already beginning to close.
worker:1.line: 'A *worker* on this dock sees every ship that dares the storm.'

sentences.en: The storm island's dock smelled of iron and rain.
sentences.cn: 风暴岛的码头闻起来有铁锈和雨水的味道。

sentences.en: A lone *worker* was patching ropes by lantern light, hands moving without pause.
'New crew?' he asked without looking up.
sentences.cn: 你是新来的船员吗？他问道，眼睛没有抬起来。

sentences.en: Old Helm nodded.
sentences.cn: 老舵点了点头。

sentences.en: The man pointed to a gap in the clouds.
sentences.cn: 那个人指向云层中的一道缝隙。

sentences.en: 'That's where the word hides,' he said.
sentences.cn: 那是这个词藏身的地方，他说。

sentences.en: 'Past the white squall.'
sentences.cn: 过了白色的急浪之后。

control:1.en: The wind hit us the moment we cleared the dock. Bell grabbed the guide-rope and pulled hard, her jaw tight. 'I have *control*,' she called over the roar. The island shuddered under our feet. Old Helm pressed a glowing word-shard into my hand and told me to hold it steady no matter what.
control:1.cnHint: 狂风中，小铃____着绳索，稳住了颤动的浮岛，老舵手将发光的碎片交给了我。
control:1.hook: The shard buzzed like a living thing against my palm.
control:1.line: 'Keep *control* of that shard or the wind takes it.'

sentences.en: The wind hit us the moment we cleared the dock.
sentences.cn: 我们刚离开码头，风就扑面而来。

sentences.en: Bell grabbed the guide-rope and pulled hard, her jaw tight.
sentences.cn: 小铃抓住导绳用力一拉，下颌紧绷。

sentences.en: 'I have *control*,' she called over the roar.
The island shuddered under our feet.
sentences.cn: 岛屿在我们脚下颤抖。

sentences.en: Old Helm pressed a glowing word-shard into my hand and told me to hold it steady no matter what.
sentences.cn: 老舵把一块发光的词碎片按进我的手心，叫我无论如何都要握稳。

product:1.en: At the centre of the storm island stood a strange market stall with no seller. Every item on the counter was a *product* of the storm itself: jars of bottled lightning, pressed cloud-cloth, and one small card glowing with a word. Silverfang reached for the card first, but Old Helm got there faster.
product:1.cnHint: 风暴岛中央有一个无人看守的摊位，每件____都来自风暴本身，其中一张卡片上发着光。
product:1.hook: Silverfang's eyes stayed on Old Helm's closed fist.
product:1.line: 'Every *product* of a storm has a price — ask Bell.'

sentences.en: At the centre of the storm island stood a strange market stall with no seller.
sentences.cn: 风暴岛的中心矗立着一个奇怪的市集摊位，里面没有卖主。

sentences.en: Every item on the counter was a *product* of the storm itself: jars of bottled lightning, pressed cloud-cloth, and one small card glowing with a word.
Silverfang reached for the card first, but Old Helm got there faster.
sentences.cn: 银牙最先伸手去拿那张卡片，但老舵动作更快。

practice:1.en: 'You have to spin the shard three times before you read it,' Bell told me, her voice patient. 'It is *practice*, not magic.' I tried. The first spin was wrong, the second was worse, but the third made the word rise in the air like smoke. Old Helm smiled for the first time all day.
practice:1.cnHint: 小铃教我用____来解读词语碎片，第三次旋转后，词语终于浮现在空气中。
practice:1.hook: The word hung there, bright and waiting, for just three seconds.
practice:1.line: 'Good *practice* makes a shard speak — do it again.'

sentences.en: 'You have to spin the shard three times before you read it,' Bell told me, her voice patient.
sentences.cn: 你得把碎片转三圈才能读它，小铃对我说，声音很耐心。

sentences.en: 'It is *practice*, not magic.'
I tried.
sentences.cn: 我试了试。

sentences.en: The first spin was wrong, the second was worse, but the third made the word rise in the air like smoke.
sentences.cn: 第一次转错了，第二次更糟，但第三次那个词就像烟雾一样升起来了。

sentences.en: Old Helm smiled for the first time all day.
sentences.cn: 老舵一整天以来第一次笑了。

environment:1.en: The storm island had its own strange *environment*: warm fog below the knees, cold air above the shoulders, and a smell like copper coins after rain. Old Helm said some words only appear in places like this. Bell wrote careful notes. I just stood still and let the strangeness settle into me.
environment:1.cnHint: 风暴岛拥有奇特的____：膝盖以下是暖雾，肩膀以上是冷空气，老舵手说有些词语只在这样的地方出现。
environment:1.hook: Then Bell's pen stopped moving, and she looked up sharply.
environment:1.line: 'This *environment* is exactly what the map described — we are close.'

sentences.en: The storm island had its own strange *environment*: warm fog below the knees, cold air above the shoulders, and a smell like copper coins after rain.
Old Helm said some words only appear in places like this.
sentences.cn: 老舵说有些词只会在这样的地方出现。

sentences.en: Bell wrote careful notes.
sentences.cn: 小铃在认真地做笔记。

sentences.en: I just stood still and let the strangeness settle into me.
sentences.cn: 我只是站着不动，让这种奇异的感觉慢慢沉入我的心里。

system:1.en: Old Helm unrolled a sheet of glowing lines on the dock. It was a *system* for reading storm patterns, each line connected to a word-fragment hidden somewhere on the island. 'Follow the lines,' he said, 'and the storm shows you the way.' Silverfang muttered that he had found the same map first.
system:1.cnHint: 老舵手展开一张发光的图纸，那是一套解读风暴的____，每条线都连接着隐藏的词语碎片。
system:1.hook: One line on the map was pulsing faster than the rest.
system:1.line: 'The *system* does not lie — trust the lines, not your fear.'

sentences.en: Old Helm unrolled a sheet of glowing lines on the dock.
sentences.cn: 老舵在码头上铺开了一张闪闪发光的线条图。

sentences.en: It was a *system* for reading storm patterns, each line connected to a word-fragment hidden somewhere on the island.
'Follow the lines,' he said, 'and the storm shows you the way.'
sentences.cn: 跟着这些线走，他说，风暴就会指引你前进的方向。

sentences.en: Silverfang muttered that he had found the same map first.
sentences.cn: 银牙嘟囔着说他早就找到了同一张地图。

natural:1.en: Bell said it was *natural* for the storm to push back when we got too close to a word-shard. 'The island keeps what it owns,' she explained, tying her hair against the wind. I nodded as if I understood. Then the sky cracked open above us and something bright fell straight toward the dock.
natural:1.cnHint: 小铃说风暴在我们靠近词语碎片时反抗是____的，就在那时，天空裂开，一道亮光落向码头。
natural:1.hook: Whatever fell from the sky landed with a sound like a bell.
natural:1.line: 'It is *natural* to be afraid here — walk toward it anyway.'

sentences.en: Bell said it was *natural* for the storm to push back when we got too close to a word-shard.
'The island keeps what it owns,' she explained, tying her hair against the wind.
sentences.cn: 岛屿守护它拥有的东西，她解释道，同时把头发扎紧以对抗风。

sentences.en: I nodded as if I understood.
sentences.cn: 我点了点头，假装自己听懂了。

sentences.en: Then the sky cracked open above us and something bright fell straight toward the dock.
sentences.cn: 然后天空在我们头顶裂开，什么明亮的东西笔直地朝码头坠落下来。

free:1.en: When the last shard clicked into our map, the storm simply stopped. The clouds parted, the wind dropped, and the stars came out all at once. Old Helm laughed — a big, full sound I had not heard before. 'We are *free* of it,' he said. Ahead, a new island glittered at the edge of the dark.
free:1.cnHint: 最后一块碎片嵌入地图后，风暴骤然停止，老舵手大笑着说我们____了，前方出现了一座新的岛屿。
free:1.hook: The new island had no name yet on any map we carried.
free:1.line: '*Free* at last — and something new is already waiting for us.'

sentences.en: When the last shard clicked into our map, the storm simply stopped.
sentences.cn: 最后一块碎片卡进地图后，风暴就这样停了。

sentences.en: The clouds parted, the wind dropped, and the stars came out all at once.
sentences.cn: 云层散开了，风停了，星星一下子全都出来了。

sentences.en: Old Helm laughed — a big, full sound I had not heard before.
sentences.cn: 老舵笑了——那是一个很大很饱满的笑声，我之前从没听过。

sentences.en: 'We are *free* of it,' he said.
Ahead, a new island glittered at the edge of the dark.
sentences.cn: 前方，一座新的岛屿在黑暗的边缘闪闪发光。

contribute:2.en: Deep in the Storm Sea, our troupe found a cracked lighthouse keeper's logbook wedged between two rocks. Old Helm read each page aloud. 'Every captain who sailed here chose to *contribute* one secret to this book,' he said softly, 'so the next crew would not sail blind.'
contribute:2.cnHint: 船员们在灯塔日志里发现，每位船长都曾____一个航行秘密。
contribute:2.hook: The last entry was written in fresh ink.
contribute:2.line: 'Each of us must *contribute* something to the log before we leave.'

sentences.en: Deep in the Storm Sea, our troupe found a cracked lighthouse keeper's logbook wedged between two rocks.
sentences.cn: 在风暴海的深处，我们的剧团发现了一本裂开的灯塔守护人日志，夹在两块岩石之间。

sentences.en: Old Helm read each page aloud.
sentences.cn: 老舵大声读着每一页。

sentences.en: 'Every captain who sailed here chose to *contribute* one secret to this book,' he said softly, 'so the next crew would not sail blind.'

share:2.en: Bell found a sealed tin box nailed to the storm-watch tower door. Inside lay a single dried biscuit and a folded note. 'Whoever is hungry, take your *share*,' the note read. Old Helm looked around at the empty tower and wondered who had left it.
share:2.cnHint: 小铃在瞭望塔门上发现了一个锡盒，里面有食物和纸条，写着每人可以拿走自己的____。
share:2.hook: A second note was hidden beneath the first.
share:2.line: 'Everyone gets a fair *share* — that is the rule of the sea.'

sentences.en: Bell found a sealed tin box nailed to the storm-watch tower door.
sentences.cn: 小铃在风暴观测塔的门上找到了一个钉着的密封铁盒。

sentences.en: Inside lay a single dried biscuit and a folded note.
sentences.cn: 里面只有一块干硬的饼干和一张折起来的纸条。

sentences.en: 'Whoever is hungry, take your *share*,' the note read.
Old Helm looked around at the empty tower and wondered who had left it.
sentences.cn: 老舵环顾四周空荡荡的塔楼，想知道是谁留下的这个。

decade:2.en: Carved into the storm-watch tower's stone wall was a long list of troupe names. Old Helm traced his finger along the lines. 'A new troupe has passed through here every *decade*,' he murmured, 'for longer than any of us have been alive.' The carving ended with a blank space.
decade:2.cnHint: 瞭望塔石壁上刻满名字，每隔一个____就有一支新队伍经过这里。
decade:2.hook: The blank space was just wide enough for one more name.
decade:2.line: 'A whole *decade* of silence — and then we arrived.'

sentences.en: Carved into the storm-watch tower's stone wall was a long list of troupe names.
sentences.cn: 在风暴观测塔的石墙上刻着一长串剧团的名字。

sentences.en: Old Helm traced his finger along the lines.
sentences.cn: 老舵用手指沿着这些线条摸过去。

sentences.en: 'A new troupe has passed through here every *decade*,' he murmured, 'for longer than any of us have been alive.'
The carving ended with a blank space.
sentences.cn: 刻字到此为止，后面是空白。

kind:2.en: Among the wreckage below the cliffs, I spotted a small glass jar filled with tiny folded papers. Each one named a different *kind* of storm: whistling storm, green-sky storm, storm-that-smells-of-lemons. Bell laughed at the last name, but Old Helm pocketed the jar without a word.
kind:2.cnHint: 小铃在残骸中找到一个罐子，里面的纸条记录着各种____的风暴名称。
kind:2.hook: One paper at the bottom had no name at all.
kind:2.line: 'I have never seen this *kind* of cloud before — stay close.'

sentences.en: Among the wreckage below the cliffs, I spotted a small glass jar filled with tiny folded papers.
sentences.cn: 在悬崖下的残骸中，我发现了一个装满折叠纸片的小玻璃罐。

sentences.en: Each one named a different *kind* of storm: whistling storm, green-sky storm, storm-that-smells-of-lemons.
Bell laughed at the last name, but Old Helm pocketed the jar without a word.
sentences.cn: 小铃听到最后一个名字笑了，但老舵什么话也没说，直接把罐子装进了口袋。

across:2.en: A rope bridge stretched *across* the widest gap between two storm-battered islands. Halfway over, Bell noticed letters burned into every third plank: a message in pieces. We had to keep walking to read it, one word at a time, the wind pulling at our coats the whole way.
across:2.cnHint: 小铃发现，要读懂那条横____峡谷的绳桥上的信息，就必须走完全程。
across:2.hook: The final plank held only a question mark.
across:2.line: 'Once we go *across*, there is no easy way back.'

sentences.en: A rope bridge stretched *across* the widest gap between two storm-battered islands.
Halfway over, Bell noticed letters burned into every third plank: a message in pieces.
sentences.cn: 走到一半时，小铃注意到每隔三块木板上都烧刻着字母——一条被分割成片段的信息。

sentences.en: We had to keep walking to read it, one word at a time, the wind pulling at our coats the whole way.
sentences.cn: 我们得继续向前才能读完它，一次一个词，风始终在扯拽我们的衣服。

factor:2.en: Old Helm spread the storm charts across the floor of our shelter and tapped a small red circle near the eastern edge. 'Wind direction is not the only *factor*,' he said. 'See this current? It bends every route. Ignore it and you drift straight into the reef.'
factor:2.cnHint: 老舵查看海图时指出，洋流是影响航线的一个重要____，不可忽视。
factor:2.hook: The red circle was not on any chart we had brought.
factor:2.line: 'Current is the hidden *factor* that most captains forget.'

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the storm charts across the floor of our shelter and tapped a small red circle near the eastern edge.
sentences.cn: 老舵把风暴图表铺在避难所的地板上，在东边边缘附近的一个小红圈上敲了敲。

sentences.en: 'Wind direction is not the only *factor*,' he said.
'See this current?
sentences.cn: 你看这股洋流？

sentences.en: It bends every route.
sentences.cn: 它改变了每条路线的方向。

sentences.en: Ignore it and you drift straight into the reef.'
sentences.cn: 忽视它，你就直接漂向礁石。

condition:2.en: The old radio set in the lighthouse crackled to life the moment Bell touched it. Static, then a clear voice listing numbers. 'It is a weather report,' Bell whispered. 'Storm *condition*: severe. Expected duration: unknown.' She wrote every word down with steady hands, then looked at Old Helm.
condition:2.cnHint: 小铃意外启动了旧收音机，听到了一段描述风暴____的气象报告。
condition:2.hook: The voice then spoke a name — our troupe's name.
condition:2.line: 'The *condition* out there is worse than it looks from here.'

sentences.en: The old radio set in the lighthouse crackled to life the moment Bell touched it.
sentences.cn: 老舵手触碰那台老旧收音机的瞬间，灯塔里的设备噼啪噼啪地活了过来。

sentences.en: Static, then a clear voice listing numbers.
sentences.cn: 先是静电噪音，然后传来一个清晰的声音在报数字。

sentences.en: 'It is a weather report,' Bell whispered.
sentences.cn: 小铃低声说，"这是天气预报。"

sentences.en: 'Storm *condition*: severe.
Expected duration: unknown.'
sentences.cn: 预计持续时间：未知。

sentences.en: She wrote every word down with steady hands, then looked at Old Helm.
sentences.cn: 她用稳定的手写下每一个字，然后抬头看向老舵。

effort:2.en: Silverfang's crew had tried to move a massive anchor blocking the harbour gate. They had left ropes, levers, and boot prints all around it. 'Every *effort* failed,' Silverfang said, leaning against the anchor with tired eyes. 'It has not moved one inch.' He glanced at Old Helm with something close to hope.
effort:2.cnHint: 银牙告诉我们，他的船员们用尽一切____，也没能移动挡住港口的大铁锚。
effort:2.hook: Old Helm smiled and pulled a small key from his coat.
effort:2.line: 'One more *effort*, together — and I think it will move.'

sentences.en: Silverfang's crew had tried to move a massive anchor blocking the harbour gate.
sentences.cn: 银牙的船员们试过移动堵在港口大门前的那个巨大铁锚。

sentences.en: They had left ropes, levers, and boot prints all around it.
sentences.cn: 他们在四周留下了绳子、杠杆和靴子踩过的痕迹。

sentences.en: 'Every *effort* failed,' Silverfang said, leaning against the anchor with tired eyes.
'It has not moved one inch.'
sentences.cn: 它一寸都没动过。

sentences.en: He glanced at Old Helm with something close to hope.
sentences.cn: 他瞥向老舵，眼神里闪烁着某种接近希望的东西。

receive:2.en: A sealed bottle bumped against the hull in the storm winds. Bell fished it out with a long hook and cracked the wax. Inside was a folded paper. 'We *receive* this and we know where the next island hides,' she said, smoothing the map with careful hands. Old Helm smiled slowly.
receive:2.cnHint: 小铃从漂流瓶中____了一张藏有下一座岛屿位置的地图。
receive:2.hook: The paper showed an island none of us had ever named.
receive:2.line: 'We *receive* this message, and the storm has already done us a favour.'

sentences.en: A sealed bottle bumped against the hull in the storm winds.
sentences.cn: 一个密封的瓶子在风暴中撞上了船的舷侧。

sentences.en: Bell fished it out with a long hook and cracked the wax.
sentences.cn: 小铃用一根长钩子把它捞出来，撬开了封蜡。

sentences.en: Inside was a folded paper.
sentences.cn: 里面有一张折好的纸。

sentences.en: 'We *receive* this and we know where the next island hides,' she said, smoothing the map with careful hands.
Old Helm smiled slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵缓缓笑了。

encourage:2.en: The wind howled and the deck tilted sharply. My hands shook on the rope. Old Helm put a steady hand on my shoulder. 'Every new member feels this,' he said, his voice warm. Those words were enough to *encourage* me, and I held on until the sky grew calm again.
encourage:2.cnHint: 老舵用温暖的话语____了我，让我在风暴中坚持下去。
encourage:2.hook: When the sky cleared, a new island floated into view.
encourage:2.line: 'I want to *encourage* you — the storm always ends, and the stars always return.'

sentences.en: The wind howled and the deck tilted sharply.
sentences.cn: 风呼啸着，甲板急剧倾斜。

sentences.en: My hands shook on the rope.
sentences.cn: 我握着绳子的手开始颤抖。

sentences.en: Old Helm put a steady hand on my shoulder.
sentences.cn: 老舵把一只稳定的手放在我的肩膀上。

sentences.en: 'Every new member feels this,' he said, his voice warm.
sentences.cn: 他说，每个新人都会这样感受，他的声音温暖而坚定。

sentences.en: Those words were enough to *encourage* me, and I held on until the sky grew calm again.

travel:2.en: Storm clouds stretched across the whole sky, but Old Helm spread the word-map flat on the table. 'Our *travel* through this region is almost done,' he said quietly, tracing the route with one finger. A single gap remained. Bell circled it in red chalk and looked up with bright eyes.
travel:2.cnHint: 老舵在地图上追踪我们的____路线，发现只剩一处空白。
travel:2.hook: That red circle pointed straight into the heart of the clouds.
travel:2.line: 'Our *travel* through the storm has earned us one last word.'

sentences.en: Storm clouds stretched across the whole sky, but Old Helm spread the word-map flat on the table.
sentences.cn: 暴风云笼罩了整片天空，但老舵把词汇地图摊平放在桌子上。

sentences.en: 'Our *travel* through this region is almost done,' he said quietly, tracing the route with one finger.
A single gap remained.
sentences.cn: 只剩下一个缺口。

sentences.en: Bell circled it in red chalk and looked up with bright eyes.
sentences.cn: 小铃用红粉笔在它周围画了个圈，抬起头时眼睛闪闪发光。

strong:2.en: The anchor chain snapped in the gale. Bell grabbed the spare and pulled hard, muscles tight, feet firm on the wet deck. The new chain held. 'She is *strong* enough for any storm this sky can throw,' Silverfang called over the wind, watching Bell with clear respect.
strong:2.cnHint: 小铃用力拉住备用锚链，证明她____到足以对抗任何风暴。
strong:2.hook: The held chain bought us time — and a new word glowed on its last link.
strong:2.line: 'You have to be *strong* here, or the wind takes everything you carry.'

sentences.en: The anchor chain snapped in the gale.
sentences.cn: 风暴中锚链断了。

sentences.en: Bell grabbed the spare and pulled hard, muscles tight, feet firm on the wet deck.
sentences.cn: 小铃抓住备用链条用力一拉，肌肉绷紧，脚在湿漉漉的甲板上站得很稳。

sentences.en: The new chain held.
sentences.cn: 新的链条撑住了。

sentences.en: 'She is *strong* enough for any storm this sky can throw,' Silverfang called over the wind, watching Bell with clear respect.

chance:2.en: Lightning lit the cloud bank for one bright moment, and I saw the outline of an island — gone before I could be sure. Old Helm said that in the storm region, such a glimpse was the only *chance* you ever got to mark a new place. I sketched its shape fast and hoped it was enough.
chance:2.cnHint: 闪电一瞬间照亮了云层，给了我____看见新岛轮廓的机会。
chance:2.hook: My rough sketch matched the word-map perfectly.
chance:2.line: 'Take every *chance* the lightning gives you — it never lights the same spot twice.'

sentences.en: Lightning lit the cloud bank for one bright moment, and I saw the outline of an island — gone before I could be sure.
sentences.cn: 闪电在一瞬间照亮了云层，我看到了一个岛屿的轮廓——还没来得及确认就消失了。

sentences.en: Old Helm said that in the storm region, such a glimpse was the only *chance* you ever got to mark a new place.
I sketched its shape fast and hoped it was enough.
sentences.cn: 我快速勾勒出它的形状，希望这样就足够了。

solve:2.en: The word-map showed two paths around the storm, but one led into rocks. Bell stared at both lines for a long quiet moment, then tapped the northern route. 'This one,' she said. 'I think I can *solve* it.' She plotted four careful turns, and every one of them was right.
solve:2.cnHint: 小铃仔细研究地图，终于____了绕过风暴的航线难题。
solve:2.hook: The fourth turn opened a gap in the clouds the size of a doorway.
solve:2.line: 'Give me a moment and I can *solve* any path this sky sets before us.'

sentences.en: The word-map showed two paths around the storm, but one led into rocks.
sentences.cn: 词汇地图显示绕过风暴有两条路线，但其中一条通向岩石。

sentences.en: Bell stared at both lines for a long quiet moment, then tapped the northern route.
sentences.cn: 小铃安静地盯着两条线看了很久，然后点了点北边的路线。

sentences.en: 'This one,' she said.
sentences.cn: 她说，就这一条。

sentences.en: 'I think I can *solve* it.'
She plotted four careful turns, and every one of them was right.
sentences.cn: 她规划出四个精确的转向，每一个都完全正确。

quite:2.en: After the worst of the storm passed, the sky turned a deep, strange green. It was *quite* unlike anything I had seen before — not green like leaves, but green like something old and knowing. Silverfang leaned on the rail and said nothing. Even he seemed small under that light.
quite:2.cnHint: 风暴过后的天空变成了一种____不寻常的深绿色，令所有人沉默。
quite:2.hook: Then a new island rose slowly out of that green glow.
quite:2.line: 'It is *quite* unlike any sky I have seen in all my years on this route.'

sentences.en: After the worst of the storm passed, the sky turned a deep, strange green.
sentences.cn: 风暴最猛烈的部分过去后，天空变成了深沉、诡异的绿色。

sentences.en: It was *quite* unlike anything I had seen before — not green like leaves, but green like something old and knowing.
Silverfang leaned on the rail and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 银牙靠在栏杆上，什么也没说。

sentences.en: Even he seemed small under that light.
sentences.cn: 连他在那种光下看起来都显得很渺小。

technology:2.en: Tucked in the storm shelter was a brass box none of us had touched before. Old Helm opened it to find small gears and a spinning dial that pointed toward hidden islands. 'Old *technology*,' he said with wonder, 'but it still knows the way.' The dial spun once and settled north.
technology:2.cnHint: 船舱里一个铜盒子里藏着一种古老的____，能指引前往隐藏岛屿的方向。
technology:2.hook: The dial pointed to a place our word-map had left completely blank.
technology:2.line: 'This *technology* was built to find what ordinary eyes cannot see.'

sentences.en: Tucked in the storm shelter was a brass box none of us had touched before.
sentences.cn: 暴风避难所里放着一个我们之前从没碰过的黄铜盒子。

sentences.en: Old Helm opened it to find small gears and a spinning dial that pointed toward hidden islands.
sentences.cn: 老舵打开它，里面是一些小齿轮和一个指向隐藏岛屿的旋转刻度盘。

sentences.en: 'Old *technology*,' he said with wonder, 'but it still knows the way.'
The dial spun once and settled north.
sentences.cn: 刻度盘转了一圈，指向了北方。

education:2.en: Inside the storm shelter, we found a carved stone tablet half-buried in sand. Old Helm brushed it clean with slow, careful hands. 'This island once held a great school,' he said. The tablet described an *education* built on curiosity — every lesson taught outdoors, under open sky. A new word glowed at its centre.
education:2.cnHint: 我们在避风所发现了一块石碑，记载着这座岛上曾有一种以好奇心为核心的____。
education:2.hook: But the school's last teacher had left one lesson unfinished.
education:2.line: 'A true *education* never fits inside four walls,' Old Helm said softly.

sentences.en: Inside the storm shelter, we found a carved stone tablet half-buried in sand.
sentences.cn: 在防风雨棚里，我们发现了一块石碑，半埋在沙子里。

sentences.en: Old Helm brushed it clean with slow, careful hands.
sentences.cn: 老舵用缓慢而仔细的手指拂去上面的灰尘。

sentences.en: 'This island once held a great school,' he said.
sentences.cn: "这座岛曾经有过一所伟大的学校，"他说。

sentences.en: The tablet described an *education* built on curiosity — every lesson taught outdoors, under open sky.
A new word glowed at its centre.
sentences.cn: 一个新的词在石碑中心闪闪发光。

scientist:2.en: A brass tube rolled out from behind a cracked wall in the old watchtower. Bell uncorked it and shook out a folded letter. It was signed by a *scientist* who had once lived on this stormy island, studying the way lightning touched the clouds. Her last line read: 'The answer drifts east.' A word shimmered on the seal.
scientist:2.cnHint: 贝尔从信筒里取出一封信，署名是曾在岛上研究闪电的一位____。
scientist:2.hook: Whatever she had discovered, she never sent the letter.
scientist:2.line: 'A *scientist* once lived here,' Bell said, eyes wide with wonder.

sentences.en: A brass tube rolled out from behind a cracked wall in the old watchtower.
sentences.cn: 一根黄铜管从旧灯塔里一道裂开的墙后滚了出来。

sentences.en: Bell uncorked it and shook out a folded letter.
sentences.cn: 小铃打开软木塞，摇出一封折叠的信。

sentences.en: It was signed by a *scientist* who had once lived on this stormy island, studying the way lightning touched the clouds.
Her last line read: 'The answer drifts east.'
sentences.cn: 她的最后一行写着："答案在东边飘浮。"

sentences.en: A word shimmered on the seal.
sentences.cn: 一个词在封蜡上闪烁。

physical:2.en: The storm had cracked the bridge between two rocks, and crossing it was a real *physical* challenge — each plank swayed and groaned under our boots. Old Helm went first, arms out for balance. When we all reached the far ledge, breathless and grinning, a word carved into the stone rail caught the starlight. We read it together.
physical:2.cnHint: 我们通过了一座摇摇晃晃的断桥，这对大家来说是一项真正的____挑战。
physical:2.hook: On the far side, something was waiting that had no business being there.
physical:2.line: 'The *physical* effort is worth every shaky step,' Old Helm called back.

sentences.en: The storm had cracked the bridge between two rocks, and crossing it was a real *physical* challenge — each plank swayed and groaned under our boots.
Old Helm went first, arms out for balance.
sentences.cn: 老舵第一个走过去，张开双臂保持平衡。

sentences.en: When we all reached the far ledge, breathless and grinning, a word carved into the stone rail caught the starlight.
sentences.cn: 当我们都喘着气、咧着嘴来到另一边的石台时，石栏杆上雕刻的一个词被星光照亮了。

sentences.en: We read it together.
sentences.cn: 我们一起读了出来。

quality:2.en: Half-hidden under storm debris, we found a box of old maps. Most were ruined, but one had survived perfectly — the ink still sharp, the paper still firm. Bell held it up to the lantern light. 'You can feel the *quality*,' she said, running her thumb along the edge. A single word was pressed into the corner like a seal, soft and golden.
quality:2.cnHint: 贝尔在残骸中发现了一张保存完好的地图，感叹其____之高。
quality:2.hook: The map showed an island none of us had ever heard of.
quality:2.line: 'Feel this paper — real *quality* lasts through any storm,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Half-hidden under storm debris, we found a box of old maps.
sentences.cn: 在风暴留下的碎片下面，我们发现了一盒老地图。

sentences.en: Most were ruined, but one had survived perfectly — the ink still sharp, the paper still firm.
sentences.cn: 大多数都损坏了，但有一张完整地保存下来了——墨迹依旧清晰，纸张依然结实。

sentences.en: Bell held it up to the lantern light.
sentences.cn: 小铃把它举到灯笼光下。

sentences.en: 'You can feel the *quality*,' she said, running her thumb along the edge.
A single word was pressed into the corner like a seal, soft and golden.
sentences.cn: 一个词被压在角落里，像一个封蜡，柔和而金灿灿的。

habit:2.en: Silverfang anchored the ship in a sheltered cove and sat on deck as the storm passed. I asked why he always did that — stayed calm while everyone else rushed about. He smiled and said it was a *habit* built over many years at sea. Then he pointed to a bottle wedged between two rocks. Inside it, a word waited like a gift.
habit:2.cnHint: 银牙告诉我，他在风暴中保持冷静是多年养成的____。
habit:2.hook: The bottle also held a rough map drawn in unfamiliar ink.
habit:2.line: 'Staying calm in a storm is just a *habit* — you can build it too,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: Silverfang anchored the ship in a sheltered cove and sat on deck as the storm passed.
sentences.cn: 银牙在一个避风的小湾停靠船只，坐在甲板上看风暴过去。

sentences.en: I asked why he always did that — stayed calm while everyone else rushed about.
sentences.cn: 我问他为什么总是这样——在别人都忙乱奔跑时保持镇定。

sentences.en: He smiled and said it was a *habit* built over many years at sea.
Then he pointed to a bottle wedged between two rocks.
sentences.cn: 然后他指向两块岩石间卡着的一个瓶子。

sentences.en: Inside it, a word waited like a gift.
sentences.cn: 瓶子里，一个词在等待，像一份礼物。

sound:2.en: We sheltered in a sea cave while thunder rolled across the sky. Then, beneath the storm's noise, I heard something else — a low, steady *sound* rising from a crack in the cave floor, almost like a hum. Bell pressed her ear to the stone and went very still. 'That,' she whispered, 'is not the wind.' A word pulsed with each note.
sound:2.cnHint: 在山洞里，我听到地面裂缝中传来一种奇特的____，贝尔认为那不是风声。
sound:2.hook: Whatever made that sound was moving closer.
sound:2.line: 'Listen — that *sound* is coming from somewhere deep below us,' Bell whispered.

sentences.en: We sheltered in a sea cave while thunder rolled across the sky.
sentences.cn: 我们躲在一个海洞里，雷声在天空滚过。

sentences.en: Then, beneath the storm's noise, I heard something else — a low, steady *sound* rising from a crack in the cave floor, almost like a hum.
Bell pressed her ear to the stone and went very still.
sentences.cn: 小铃把耳朵贴在石头上，一动不动。

sentences.en: 'That,' she whispered, 'is not the wind.'
sentences.cn: "那，"她低声说，"不是风。"

sentences.en: A word pulsed with each note.
sentences.cn: 一个词随着每个音符搏动。

average:2.en: Old Helm spread three old journals on the shelter table and read the wind records aloud. Most days logged were rough, but nothing extreme. 'By any *average*,' he said, tapping the numbers, 'this is the stormiest zone on the whole map.' He closed the last journal and a folded page slipped out — a word written in blue ink, circled twice.
average:2.cnHint: 老赫姆查阅航海日志，指出这片区域的风暴频率远超____水平。
average:2.hook: The folded page also showed a route no map had ever included.
average:2.line: 'Above every *average* I have ever measured — this zone is wild,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Old Helm spread three old journals on the shelter table and read the wind records aloud.
sentences.cn: 老舵在棚子的桌子上铺开三本旧日志，大声读出风的记录。

sentences.en: Most days logged were rough, but nothing extreme.
sentences.cn: 记录的大多数日子天气都很恶劣，但没有特别极端的。

sentences.en: 'By any *average*,' he said, tapping the numbers, 'this is the stormiest zone on the whole map.'
He closed the last journal and a folded page slipped out — a word written in blue ink, circled twice.
sentences.cn: 他合上最后一本日志，一页折叠的纸从里面滑出来——一个用蓝墨水写的词，圆圈标记了两次。

body:2.en: At low tide, a stone door appeared at the base of the cliff. We pushed it open and found a small dry room. At its centre stood a model of the whole island chain — each floating island shaped in clay, arranged around a hollow where a single bright word rested. 'The *body* of the map,' Bell breathed. 'We found its heart.'
body:2.cnHint: 退潮后，我们发现了一个密室，里面藏着整个岛链模型的____部分。
body:2.hook: One island in the model was still warm to the touch.
body:2.line: 'This clay model is the *body* of every map we have been chasing,' Bell said.

sentences.en: At low tide, a stone door appeared at the base of the cliff.
sentences.cn: 在退潮时，一道石门出现在悬崖底部。

sentences.en: We pushed it open and found a small dry room.
sentences.cn: 我们推开它，发现了一个小小的干燥房间。

sentences.en: At its centre stood a model of the whole island chain — each floating island shaped in clay, arranged around a hollow where a single bright word rested.
sentences.cn: 房间中央矗立着整个岛链的模型——每个漂浮的岛都用粘土塑成，围绕一个空心摆放，里面放着一个闪亮的词。

sentences.en: 'The *body* of the map,' Bell breathed.
'We found its heart.'
sentences.cn: "我们找到了它的心脏。"

personal:2.en: Among the storm wreckage on the lower deck, Bell found a small box, half-buried under wet rope. She held it up to the lantern light. A name was carved on the lid — her own. Inside lay a folded note. Whatever was written there, she kept it *personal*, folding it quietly against her chest.
personal:2.cnHint: 小铃在残骸中发现了一个刻有自己名字的盒子，她把其中的内容____地藏在心里。
personal:2.hook: Whose hand had carved that name before the storm?
personal:2.line: 'This is *personal* — I will read it alone,' Bell said softly.

sentences.en: Among the storm wreckage on the lower deck, Bell found a small box, half-buried under wet rope.
sentences.cn: 在下甲板的风暴残骸中，小铃发现了一个小盒子，半埋在湿漉漉的绳索下。

sentences.en: She held it up to the lantern light.
sentences.cn: 她把它举到灯笼光下。

sentences.en: A name was carved on the lid — her own.
sentences.cn: 盖子上刻着一个名字——她自己的。

sentences.en: Inside lay a folded note.
sentences.cn: 里面放着一张折叠的纸条。

sentences.en: Whatever was written there, she kept it *personal*, folding it quietly against her chest.

rather:2.en: The storm had bent the old signal mast sideways. Old Helm stood before it, stroking his beard. We had rope, and I expected him to pull the mast straight. He looked at the broken base *rather* carefully, then shook his head. 'We build a new one,' he said. 'Better than fixing a broken thing.'
rather:2.cnHint: 老舵____仔细地检查了断裂的信号桅杆，决定重新建造一根。
rather:2.hook: But what signal had the old mast been trying to send?
rather:2.line: 'Look *rather* closely — the base is cracked clean through,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: The storm had bent the old signal mast sideways.
sentences.cn: 风暴把老信号桅杆弯成了歪斜。

sentences.en: Old Helm stood before it, stroking his beard.
sentences.cn: 老舵站在它面前，摸着胡须。

sentences.en: We had rope, and I expected him to pull the mast straight.
sentences.cn: 我们有绳子，我以为他会把桅杆拉直。

sentences.en: He looked at the broken base *rather* carefully, then shook his head.
'We build a new one,' he said.
sentences.cn: "我们造一个新的，"他说。

sentences.en: 'Better than fixing a broken thing.'
sentences.cn: "总比修一个坏掉的东西要好。"

instead:2.en: Bell had plotted a course straight through the storm's eye, marked in red on the chart. Silverfang studied it, then drew a wide curve around the dark clouds *instead*. 'The eye moves,' she said simply, rolling the chart back up. Outside, thunder answered as if it agreed with her.
instead:2.cnHint: 小铃原本画了一条穿越风暴的路线，但银牙____选择了绕行的方向。
instead:2.hook: The storm's eye was moving — but toward them or away?
instead:2.line: 'Take the long way around *instead* — the eye shifts,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: Bell had plotted a course straight through the storm's eye, marked in red on the chart.
sentences.cn: 小铃在海图上用红色标出了一条直穿风暴眼的航线。

sentences.en: Silverfang studied it, then drew a wide curve around the dark clouds *instead*.
'The eye moves,' she said simply, rolling the chart back up.
sentences.cn: 银牙简单地说了一句，"风眼会移动，"然后把海图卷了起来。

sentences.en: Outside, thunder answered as if it agreed with her.
sentences.cn: 外面的雷声响起，仿佛在赞同她的话。

performance:2.en: Old Helm gathered us on deck while rain still spat at the sails. He pulled out a worn map fragment and held it to the sky. Reading a storm chart in the wind was no simple act — his calm, steady hands made it look easy. That quiet *performance* of confidence settled every nervous heart on deck.
performance:2.cnHint: 老舵在风雨中镇定读图的____，让船上每一颗不安的心都平静下来。
performance:2.hook: But Old Helm's hands, I noticed, were trembling just slightly.
performance:2.line: 'That calm *performance* of his — do you think he was scared too?' Bell whispered.

sentences.en: Old Helm gathered us on deck while rain still spat at the sails.
sentences.cn: 老舵在雨还在打帆的时候把我们聚集在甲板上。

sentences.en: He pulled out a worn map fragment and held it to the sky.
sentences.cn: 他拿出一张磨损的地图碎片，举向天空。

sentences.en: Reading a storm chart in the wind was no simple act — his calm, steady hands made it look easy.
sentences.cn: 在风中读风暴图表不是简单的事——他那平静而稳定的手让一切看起来轻而易举。

sentences.en: That quiet *performance* of confidence settled every nervous heart on deck.

percent:2.en: Bell checked the rigging with a practiced eye after the worst of the storm had passed. She pulled each line, listening to its tone. 'Sixty *percent* of the upper ropes need replacing,' she told Old Helm, her voice steady. He nodded slowly. The ship had held — but only just.
percent:2.cnHint: 小铃检查索具后告诉老舵，有六十____的绳索需要更换。
percent:2.hook: And the ropes holding the word-chart safe — were they among the sixty?
percent:2.line: 'Sixty *percent* of these lines won't last another storm,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Bell checked the rigging with a practiced eye after the worst of the storm had passed.
sentences.cn: 暴风雨过去后，小铃用娴熟的眼光检查了索具。

sentences.en: She pulled each line, listening to its tone.
sentences.cn: 她逐一拉动每条绳索，听着它们的声音。

sentences.en: 'Sixty *percent* of the upper ropes need replacing,' she told Old Helm, her voice steady.
He nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵慢慢点了点头。

sentences.en: The ship had held — but only just.
sentences.cn: 船撑住了——但只是勉强。

achieve:2.en: Silverfang had tried three times to anchor in the churning bay below the storm clouds. Each time the anchor dragged. On the fourth try, she changed the angle and let the chain run longer. The hold caught. What one careful adjustment could *achieve* surprised even her, and a rare smile crossed her face.
achieve:2.cnHint: 经过几次失败，银牙调整了角度，终于____了稳定抛锚。
achieve:2.hook: The anchor held — but something below had shifted in the dark water.
achieve:2.line: 'A small change in angle can *achieve* what pure force cannot,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: Silverfang had tried three times to anchor in the churning bay below the storm clouds.
sentences.cn: 银牙在风暴乌云下翻腾的海湾里试了三次下锚。

sentences.en: Each time the anchor dragged.
sentences.cn: 每一次锚都拖动了。

sentences.en: On the fourth try, she changed the angle and let the chain run longer.
sentences.cn: 第四次，她改变了角度，让铁链跑得更长。

sentences.en: The hold caught.
sentences.cn: 锚抓住了。

sentences.en: What one careful adjustment could *achieve* surprised even her, and a rare smile crossed her face.

challenge:2.en: The narrow passage between two storm-dark cliffs was the only way forward. Old Helm stared at it for a long moment, then turned to face us all. 'I will not pretend this is easy,' he said quietly. He called it a *challenge* worth meeting, and in his voice was something that made us believe him.
challenge:2.cnHint: 老舵直视那条险峻的通道，称它为一次值得迎接的____。
challenge:2.hook: The cliffs were close — and one hidden rock could end everything.
challenge:2.line: 'Every *challenge* worth meeting asks something real of you,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: The narrow passage between two storm-dark cliffs was the only way forward.
sentences.cn: 两座风暴昏暗的悬崖之间有一条狭窄的通道，那是唯一的出路。

sentences.en: Old Helm stared at it for a long moment, then turned to face us all.
sentences.cn: 老舵盯着它看了很久，然后转身面向我们所有人。

sentences.en: 'I will not pretend this is easy,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: "我不会假装这很容易，"他轻声说。

sentences.en: He called it a *challenge* worth meeting, and in his voice was something that made us believe him.

power:2.en: The storm's last wave struck the hull hard, and every lantern on board went dark. We stood in cold blackness while the ship groaned. Then, one by one, the word-fragments on the map table began to glow on their own, soft and gold. Whatever *power* lived inside them, it was stronger than the storm.
power:2.cnHint: 风暴熄灭了所有灯火，但地图碎片自发散发出光芒，展示出它们神秘的____。
power:2.hook: The glow spelled something — a name none of us recognised.
power:2.line: 'The *power* in these words — I think they are trying to guide us,' Bell said.

sentences.en: The storm's last wave struck the hull hard, and every lantern on board went dark.
sentences.cn: 暴风雨的最后一浪狠狠击中了船体，船上所有的灯笼都灭了。

sentences.en: We stood in cold blackness while the ship groaned.
sentences.cn: 我们站在冷冷的黑暗里，船在呻吟。

sentences.en: Then, one by one, the word-fragments on the map table began to glow on their own, soft and gold.
sentences.cn: 然后，地图台上的字片一个接一个地自己亮了起来，柔和的金黄色。

sentences.en: Whatever *power* lived inside them, it was stronger than the storm.

key:2.en: Inside the hollow of a storm-cracked buoy, I found a small brass *key* tied to a scrap of paper. The paper showed a door shape drawn in ink — a door none of us had seen yet. Old Helm held it to the light and nodded slowly, as if he had been waiting for exactly this.
key:2.cnHint: 我在浮标内发现了一把小小的____，上面附着一张画有门形图案的纸条。
key:2.hook: Somewhere on this island, a door is already listening.
key:2.line: Old Helm: 'This *key* was meant to find us, not the other way around.'

sentences.en: Inside the hollow of a storm-cracked buoy, I found a small brass *key* tied to a scrap of paper.
The paper showed a door shape drawn in ink — a door none of us had seen yet.
sentences.cn: 纸上用墨水画了一扇门的形状——一扇我们都没见过的门。

sentences.en: Old Helm held it to the light and nodded slowly, as if he had been waiting for exactly this.
sentences.cn: 老舵把它举向光线，慢慢点了点头，仿佛他一直在等待正是这个。

issue:2.en: Bell spread the torn chart across the deck and pointed to a blank patch near the storm's edge. 'This is the real *issue*,' she said. No map, no word, no guide — just open sky and wild wind beyond. Old Helm crossed his arms and studied the blank space as if it might speak.
issue:2.cnHint: 小铃指着海图上的空白区域，说出了我们面临的真正____。
issue:2.hook: The blank patch on the map was not empty — it was waiting.
issue:2.line: Bell: 'The *issue* is not the storm — it is what the storm is hiding.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the torn chart across the deck and pointed to a blank patch near the storm's edge.
sentences.cn: 小铃把撕裂的海图铺在甲板上，指向风暴边缘附近的一片空白。

sentences.en: 'This is the real *issue*,' she said.
No map, no word, no guide — just open sky and wild wind beyond.
sentences.cn: 没有地图，没有文字，没有向导——只有开阔的天空和beyond的狂风。

sentences.en: Old Helm crossed his arms and studied the blank space as if it might speak.
sentences.cn: 老舵交叉双臂，研究着这片空白，仿佛它可能会说话。

against:2.en: The wind pushed hard *against* the hull all night, and by morning three of our word-lanterns had gone dark. I pressed my back against the mast and held the last lantern with both hands. Old Helm stood at the bow, perfectly still, letting the storm do its worst.
against:2.cnHint: 狂风整夜____船身猛吹，我们的文字灯笼一盏接一盏地熄灭。
against:2.hook: Old Helm turned and smiled — which was somehow worse than the storm.
against:2.line: Old Helm: 'Everything worth keeping has been tested *against* the wind.'

sentences.en: The wind pushed hard *against* the hull all night, and by morning three of our word-lanterns had gone dark.
I pressed my back against the mast and held the last lantern with both hands.
sentences.cn: 我把后背贴在桅杆上，用双手紧紧握住最后一盏灯笼。

sentences.en: Old Helm stood at the bow, perfectly still, letting the storm do its worst.
sentences.cn: 老舵站在船首，一动不动，任由暴风雨尽其所能。

matter:2.en: Silverfang pulled alongside our vessel just as the clouds broke open. He tossed a sealed tube across the gap — inside was a single folded note. 'Read it,' he called over the roar of rain. The *matter* written there was simple: someone had already reached the next island before any of us.
matter:2.cnHint: 银牙抛来一个密封筒，里面那张纸条上所写的____让我们震惊。
matter:2.hook: A boot print in fresh mud does not stay fresh for long.
matter:2.line: Silverfang: 'The *matter* is simple — we are not alone out here.'

sentences.en: Silverfang pulled alongside our vessel just as the clouds broke open.
sentences.cn: 就在乌云散开的时候，银牙靠近了我们的船。

sentences.en: He tossed a sealed tube across the gap — inside was a single folded note.
sentences.cn: 他甩过来一个密封的管子——里面是一张折叠的纸条。

sentences.en: 'Read it,' he called over the roar of rain.
sentences.cn: "读一下，"他在雨声中喊道。

sentences.en: The *matter* written there was simple: someone had already reached the next island before any of us.

raise:2.en: Bell climbed to the top of the signal mast and began to *raise* a flag made from stitched word-scraps. Each scrap was a place we had already passed through. The flag caught the wind and opened wide, bright against the grey sky — a moving map of everywhere we had been.
raise:2.cnHint: 小铃爬上桅杆，将一面由文字碎片缝制而成的旗子____起来。
raise:2.hook: On the far shore, something answered with a light of its own.
raise:2.line: Bell: 'We *raise* this flag so the next troupe knows the road is real.'

sentences.en: Bell climbed to the top of the signal mast and began to *raise* a flag made from stitched word-scraps.
Each scrap was a place we had already passed through.
sentences.cn: 每一片布料都是我们已经经过的地方。

sentences.en: The flag caught the wind and opened wide, bright against the grey sky — a moving map of everywhere we had been.
sentences.cn: 旗帜被风吹起并张开了，在灰色天空下闪闪发光——一张移动的地图，记录了我们曾经去过的每一个地方。

option:2.en: The storm had split our usual route in two: south meant shallow rocks, north meant thick fog with no stars to read. I looked at Old Helm and waited. He studied both horizons for a long moment. 'There is a third *option*,' he said quietly, pointing straight up into the open sky above the clouds.
option:2.cnHint: 航路被风暴截断，老舵却提出了我们都没想到的第三个____。
option:2.hook: None of us had ever sailed upward before.
option:2.line: Old Helm: 'When every *option* looks wrong, look for the one no one named yet.'

sentences.en: The storm had split our usual route in two: south meant shallow rocks, north meant thick fog with no stars to read.
sentences.cn: 暴风雨把我们通常的路线分成了两条：向南意味着浅滩礁石，向北意味着浓雾，没有星星可以读。

sentences.en: I looked at Old Helm and waited.
sentences.cn: 我看着老舵等待。

sentences.en: He studied both horizons for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 他长时间地研究了两个地平线。

sentences.en: 'There is a third *option*,' he said quietly, pointing straight up into the open sky above the clouds.

society:2.en: Tucked inside the storm-shelter hut, we found a shelf of small books — a record kept by earlier travellers. They had called themselves the Drifting Word *Society*, and they had mapped every floating island in this region before the great storm swallowed their trail. Old Helm ran a finger along the spines, his eyes bright.
society:2.cnHint: 我们在避风小屋里发现了一批旅行者留下的书籍，记录着一个叫"漂流文字____"的团体。
society:2.hook: The last book on the shelf had our troupe's name already written inside.
society:2.line: Old Helm: 'Every *society* of wanderers leaves a door open for the next one.'

sentences.en: Tucked inside the storm-shelter hut, we found a shelf of small books — a record kept by earlier travellers.
sentences.cn: 挤在风暴避难所小屋里，我们找到了一架小书——早期旅行者留下的记录。

sentences.en: They had called themselves the Drifting Word *Society*, and they had mapped every floating island in this region before the great storm swallowed their trail.
Old Helm ran a finger along the spines, his eyes bright.
sentences.cn: 老舵用手指沿着书脊滑动，眼睛闪闪发光。

whole:2.en: When the final storm-cloud rolled away, the *whole* chain of islands came into view at once — seven peaks lined up like stepping stones across the morning sky. I had only ever seen them one by one. Seeing all of them together felt like reading a sentence I had only ever heard one word at a time.
whole:2.cnHint: 风暴散去后，____列岛同时出现在我们眼前，美得令人屏息。
whole:2.hook: Bell whispered a name for the chain — and the islands seemed to lean in.
whole:2.line: Bell: 'Only when you see the *whole* picture does the journey make sense.'

sentences.en: When the final storm-cloud rolled away, the *whole* chain of islands came into view at once — seven peaks lined up like stepping stones across the morning sky.
I had only ever seen them one by one.
sentences.cn: 我以前只见过它们一个接一个。

sentences.en: Seeing all of them together felt like reading a sentence I had only ever heard one word at a time.
sentences.cn: 一次看到所有的它们，感觉像在读一个我曾经只听过一个词一次的句子。

nearly:2.en: The old bottle had been wedged inside a hollow rock at the edge of Storm Reach for who knows how long. Bell pulled it free and unrolled the note inside. 'This map fragment is *nearly* complete,' she said, tracing the faded lines with one careful finger. One more piece and the whole northern passage would open.
nearly:2.cnHint: 小铃从礁石中取出一张旧地图碎片，发现它____完整，只差最后一块拼图。
nearly:2.hook: But the final piece was on the rival ship.
nearly:2.line: 'This map is *nearly* whole — one more word and we sail north.'

sentences.en: The old bottle had been wedged inside a hollow rock at the edge of Storm Reach for who knows how long.
sentences.cn: 那只老瓶子不知道被楔在风暴边缘的空心石头里多久了。

sentences.en: Bell pulled it free and unrolled the note inside.
sentences.cn: 小铃把它拔出来，展开了里面的纸条。

sentences.en: 'This map fragment is *nearly* complete,' she said, tracing the faded lines with one careful finger.
One more piece and the whole northern passage would open.
sentences.cn: 再找到一块，整条北边的通道就会打开。

wrong:2.en: I found the message carved into the underside of a drifting plank — but something felt *wrong* the moment I read it. The directions pointed east, yet every wind on Storm Reach blows west. Old Helm studied the carving and nodded slowly. 'Someone wrote this to mislead,' he said. 'We go the other way.'
wrong:2.cnHint: 我在漂流木板上发现了一条刻字信息，但方向似乎是____的，老舵识破了其中的圈套。
wrong:2.hook: Whoever carved it was still watching us.
wrong:2.line: 'The directions are *wrong* — trust the wind, not the wood.'

sentences.en: I found the message carved into the underside of a drifting plank — but something felt *wrong* the moment I read it.
The directions pointed east, yet every wind on Storm Reach blows west.
sentences.cn: 方向指向东边，可风暴海域的风全是从西边吹来的。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied the carving and nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵研究了一下这些刻痕，慢慢点了点头。

sentences.en: 'Someone wrote this to mislead,' he said.
sentences.cn: "有人故意写这个来误导我们，"他说。

sentences.en: 'We go the other way.'
sentences.cn: "我们往另一个方向走。"

variety:2.en: The chest we pulled up from the shallow ledge held a *variety* of small objects: a brass compass, three dried seeds, a folded cloth covered in tiny symbols, and one glowing word-fragment that pulsed like a slow heartbeat. Bell spread them on the deck. Each one pointed to a different island. Old Helm smiled. 'Choices,' he said.
variety:2.cnHint: 我们打捞上来一个箱子，里面装着____各异的物品，每件都指向一座不同的岛屿。
variety:2.hook: We could only carry one island's secret at a time.
variety:2.line: 'What a *variety* of clues — the storm kept them safe for us.'

sentences.en: The chest we pulled up from the shallow ledge held a *variety* of small objects: a brass compass, three dried seeds, a folded cloth covered in tiny symbols, and one glowing word-fragment that pulsed like a slow heartbeat.
Bell spread them on the deck.
sentences.cn: 小铃把这些东西铺在甲板上。

sentences.en: Each one pointed to a different island.
sentences.cn: 每一件都指向一个不同的岛屿。

sentences.en: Old Helm smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵笑了。

sentences.en: 'Choices,' he said.
sentences.cn: "选择，"他说。

clear:2.en: After the squall passed, the sky above Storm Reach turned perfectly *clear*, and the stars came out all at once like someone had switched on every lamp in the world. Bell pointed to a formation low on the horizon. 'That pattern matches the symbol on our fragment,' she said quietly. The next island was already drawing us toward it.
clear:2.cnHint: 暴风雨过后天空变得____，小铃在星象中找到了与地图碎片吻合的图案。
clear:2.hook: The stars would not stay readable for long.
clear:2.line: 'The sky is finally *clear* — read the stars before the clouds return.'

sentences.en: After the squall passed, the sky above Storm Reach turned perfectly *clear*, and the stars came out all at once like someone had switched on every lamp in the world.
Bell pointed to a formation low on the horizon.
sentences.cn: 小铃指向地平线低处的一个星群。

sentences.en: 'That pattern matches the symbol on our fragment,' she said quietly.
sentences.cn: "这个图案和我们纸片上的符号一样，"她轻声说。

sentences.en: The next island was already drawing us toward it.
sentences.cn: 下一个岛屿已经在把我们往那边拽了。

gain:2.en: Silverfang had been circling Storm Reach for two days, waiting. Old Helm watched the rival ship through his long glass and shook his head. 'He thinks patience is a *gain*,' he said. 'But we already have the fragment.' I looked at the glowing word in my hand and felt the deck hum beneath my feet, eager to move.
gain:2.cnHint: 银牙的船在风暴海域徘徊等待，但老舵说我们已有所____，无需再等。
gain:2.hook: Silverfang's ship suddenly changed course — straight toward us.
gain:2.line: 'Patience is a *gain* only if you know what you are waiting for.'

sentences.en: Silverfang had been circling Storm Reach for two days, waiting.
sentences.cn: 银牙在风暴海域周围转圈已经两天了，在等待。

sentences.en: Old Helm watched the rival ship through his long glass and shook his head.
sentences.cn: 老舵用长筒镜观察着对方的船，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: 'He thinks patience is a *gain*,' he said.
'But we already have the fragment.'
sentences.cn: "但我们已经有纸片了。"

sentences.en: I looked at the glowing word in my hand and felt the deck hum beneath my feet, eager to move.
sentences.cn: 我看着手里那个发光的字，感觉甲板在脚下嗡嗡作响，迫不及待想要启航。

maybe:2.en: The sealed jar had drifted all the way to our hull, knocking softly until Bell fished it out. Inside was a single strip of paper with five words on it and a rough sketch of an arch. '*Maybe* it is a gate,' I said, holding the sketch up to the starlight. Old Helm took it from me, turned it over, and smiled at something only he could see.
maybe:2.cnHint: 一个漂来的密封瓶子里有张纸条和一幅拱门素描，我猜____是某个门，老舵似乎看出了更多。
maybe:2.hook: His smile told me the arch was already behind us.
maybe:2.line: '*Maybe* the gate was never locked — only forgotten.'

sentences.en: The sealed jar had drifted all the way to our hull, knocking softly until Bell fished it out.
sentences.cn: 那个密封的罐子一路漂到了我们的船舷，轻轻敲打着，直到小铃把它捞出来。

sentences.en: Inside was a single strip of paper with five words on it and a rough sketch of an arch. '*Maybe* it is a gate,' I said, holding the sketch up to the starlight.
Old Helm took it from me, turned it over, and smiled at something only he could see.
sentences.cn: 老舵从我手里接过去，翻了个面，对着只有他才能看到的东西笑了。

huge:2.en: The word-fragment we recovered pulsed once and projected a soft light onto the mist. The shape that appeared was *huge* — an island three times the size of any we had visited, with cliffs like dark towers and a plateau glowing faintly at its crown. Nobody spoke for a moment. Then Bell added it to the map and the map shivered with excitement.
huge:2.cnHint: 碎片投出的光芒揭示了一座____的岛屿，比我们见过的任何地方都大，地图似乎也因此颤动起来。
huge:2.hook: Something on that plateau was already sending signals back.
huge:2.line: 'That island is *huge* — we will need every word we have to reach it.'

sentences.en: The word-fragment we recovered pulsed once and projected a soft light onto the mist.
sentences.cn: 我们打捞上来的那个字投射出柔和的光，照在雾气上。

sentences.en: The shape that appeared was *huge* — an island three times the size of any we had visited, with cliffs like dark towers and a plateau glowing faintly at its crown.
Nobody spoke for a moment.
sentences.cn: 没人说话。

sentences.en: Then Bell added it to the map and the map shivered with excitement.
sentences.cn: 然后小铃把它加到地图上，地图兴奋得颤抖起来。

diet:2.en: Tucked inside the drifting crate was a handwritten notebook. Most pages were weather notes, but one page listed the crew's daily *diet*: dried fruit, rainwater, and a small portion of something called sky-grain. A pressed sample fell from between the pages — pale gold, still faintly sweet. Bell tasted a single grain and said it came from an island none of our maps had ever named.
diet:2.cnHint: 漂流箱里有本笔记，记录着一支神秘船队的日常____，小铃从中发现了一种来自未知岛屿的奇特粮食。
diet:2.hook: The island that grew sky-grain was not on any map — yet.
diet:2.line: 'Their *diet* tells us everything — this grain grows nowhere we have been.'

sentences.en: Tucked inside the drifting crate was a handwritten notebook.
sentences.cn: 漂来的木板箱里面装着一本手写笔记本。

sentences.en: Most pages were weather notes, but one page listed the crew's daily *diet*: dried fruit, rainwater, and a small portion of something called sky-grain.
A pressed sample fell from between the pages — pale gold, still faintly sweet.
sentences.cn: 一个压干的样本从书页间掉了出来——淡金色，还隐隐散发甜味。

sentences.en: Bell tasted a single grain and said it came from an island none of our maps had ever named.
sentences.cn: 小铃尝了一粒，说它来自我们的地图上从没有过的一个岛屿。

animal:2.en: The old chest washed up on the reef shelf just before dawn. Inside, wrapped in oilskin, was a map tile stitched with thread into the shape of a running *animal* — four legs, long tail, ears flat against the wind. Bell held it to the starlight. 'This is the Isle of Beasts,' she said softly. Old Helm smiled and added it to the chain.
animal:2.cnHint: 贝尔在漂来的箱子里发现了一块绣着____图案的地图碎片。
animal:2.hook: Somewhere beyond the clouds, something large was moving.
animal:2.line: 'Every *animal* on that isle knows the way through the storm,' Bell said.

sentences.en: The old chest washed up on the reef shelf just before dawn.
sentences.cn: 那只老木箱在天亮前冲上了礁石架。

sentences.en: Inside, wrapped in oilskin, was a map tile stitched with thread into the shape of a running *animal* — four legs, long tail, ears flat against the wind.
Bell held it to the starlight.
sentences.cn: 小铃把它举向星光。

sentences.en: 'This is the Isle of Beasts,' she said softly.
sentences.cn: "这是野兽岛，"她轻声说。

sentences.en: Old Helm smiled and added it to the chain.
sentences.cn: 老舵笑了，把它加到了这条链上。

goal:2.en: A brass tube rolled out from under the chart table and cracked open on the deck. Inside was a rolled note in a stranger's handwriting. It named one island and one task: reach the Eye of the Gale before the tide turns. Old Helm read it twice. 'That,' he said, tapping the paper, 'is now our *goal*.' The crew straightened without a word.
goal:2.cnHint: 一张神秘纸条让老舵把一座岛屿定为了全队的____。
goal:2.line: 'A *goal* without a deadline is just a wish,' Old Helm said quietly.

sentences.en: A brass tube rolled out from under the chart table and cracked open on the deck.
sentences.cn: 一根黄铜管从海图桌下面滚出来，在甲板上裂开了。

sentences.en: Inside was a rolled note in a stranger's handwriting.
sentences.cn: 里面是一张用陌生笔迹写的纸条。

sentences.en: It named one island and one task: reach the Eye of the Gale before the tide turns.
sentences.cn: 它指名了一个岛屿和一个任务：在潮水转向前到达风眼。

sentences.en: Old Helm read it twice.
sentences.cn: 老舵读了两遍。

sentences.en: 'That,' he said, tapping the paper, 'is now our *goal*.'
The crew straightened without a word.
sentences.cn: 船员们默不作声地站直了身子。

adult:2.en: The message was sealed with blue wax and addressed to no one. Inside, the words were short: only an *adult* who has steered through a real storm may open the lower hatch. I looked at my hands, still shaking from last night's squall. Old Helm nodded at me. 'You qualify,' he said. The hatch clicked open.
adult:2.cnHint: 一条封印的信息说只有经历过真正风暴的____才能打开下面的舱门。
adult:2.hook: Whatever was in the hatch had been waiting a very long time.
adult:2.line: 'You are an *adult* the moment the storm stops scaring you less,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: The message was sealed with blue wax and addressed to no one.
sentences.cn: 信件是用蓝蜡封的，没有地址。

sentences.en: Inside, the words were short: only an *adult* who has steered through a real storm may open the lower hatch.
I looked at my hands, still shaking from last night's squall.
sentences.cn: 我低头看看自己的手，还在为昨晚的风暴颤抖。

sentences.en: Old Helm nodded at me.
sentences.cn: 老舵朝我点了点头。

sentences.en: 'You qualify,' he said.
sentences.cn: "你符合条件，"他说。

sentences.en: The hatch clicked open.
sentences.cn: 舱门咔一声打开了。

poor:2.en: Tucked behind the broken mast lantern was a small tin box. Inside lay a single map shard and a faded note: 'Left by a *poor* sailor who had nothing else to give.' The words were worn but the shard was perfect, its edges locking neatly into our growing map. Bell pressed it into place. A new coastline appeared.
poor:2.cnHint: 一个____水手留下的地图碎片，藏在破损的桅杆灯后面。
poor:2.hook: The name on the note matched a grave marker Bell had seen two islands back.
poor:2.line: 'A *poor* man with a good map is richer than he knows,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: Tucked behind the broken mast lantern was a small tin box.
sentences.cn: 破裂的桅灯后面塞着一个小铁盒。

sentences.en: Inside lay a single map shard and a faded note: 'Left by a *poor* sailor who had nothing else to give.'
The words were worn but the shard was perfect, its edges locking neatly into our growing map.
sentences.cn: 这些字磨损了但纸片完好无损，边缘完美地锁进了我们不断拼接的地图里。

sentences.en: Bell pressed it into place.
sentences.cn: 小铃把它按了进去。

sentences.en: A new coastline appeared.
sentences.cn: 一条新的海岸线出现了。

price:2.en: The sealed jar was floating inside the cargo net, bumping gently against the hull. A note tied to its neck read: 'The word inside is yours — but the *price* is one clear memory given to the wind.' Old Helm uncorked it without hesitation and closed his eyes. The jar glowed, then went dark. A new map shard drifted down into his palm.
price:2.cnHint: 一个漂浮的密封罐子里装着地图碎片，但得到它需要付出一定的____。
price:2.hook: Old Helm never said which memory he gave away.
price:2.line: 'Every word has a *price*; this one asked for something we could afford,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: The sealed jar was floating inside the cargo net, bumping gently against the hull.
sentences.cn: 密封的罐子浮在货网里，轻轻地撞击着船体。
