Old Helm uncorked it without hesitation and closed his eyes.
sentences.cn: 老舵毫不犹豫地打开了罐子，闭上了眼睛。

sentences.en: The jar glowed, then went dark.
sentences.cn: 罐子发出光芒，随后陷入黑暗。

sentences.en: A new map shard drifted down into his palm.
sentences.cn: 一片新的地图碎片飘落到他的掌心。

type:2.en: The signal lantern on the far reef blinked in a pattern none of us knew. Bell copied it down, dot by dot. 'It is a *type* of code used by the deep-water pilots,' she said, spreading her notes on the deck. 'Each blink is a letter; each letter is part of a place name.' We leaned in together as the island's true name slowly appeared.
type:2.cnHint: 远处礁石上的信号灯闪烁着一种特殊____的密码，贝尔正在破译。
type:2.hook: The final letter made Bell go very still.
type:2.line: 'I have seen this *type* of signal only once before, and that island no longer exists,' Bell said.

sentences.en: The signal lantern on the far reef blinked in a pattern none of us knew.
sentences.cn: 远处礁石上的信号灯闪烁着一种我们都不认识的模式。

sentences.en: Bell copied it down, dot by dot.
sentences.cn: 小铃一点一点地记录下来。

sentences.en: 'It is a *type* of code used by the deep-water pilots,' she said, spreading her notes on the deck.
'Each blink is a letter; each letter is part of a place name.'

sentences.en: We leaned in together as the island's true name slowly appeared.
sentences.cn: 我们一起靠近，岛屿真正的名字慢慢显现出来。

sense:2.en: The compass needle spun once, then stopped pointing north — it pointed down. Old Helm knelt and pressed his ear to the deck. 'I can *sense* a hollow space below,' he said, 'about the size of a map chest.' We shifted three planks aside. There it was: a locked box with a fresh storm-lily pressed under the latch, still warm.
sense:2.cnHint: 老舵凭借某种____察觉到甲板下方藏着一个空间。
sense:2.hook: The storm-lily only blooms at the centre of a living storm.
sense:2.line: 'You will develop a *sense* for hidden things — the islands teach it,' Old Helm told me.

sentences.en: The compass needle spun once, then stopped pointing north — it pointed down.
sentences.cn: 指南针的针转了一圈，然后停止了——它不再指向北方，而是指向下方。

sentences.en: Old Helm knelt and pressed his ear to the deck.
sentences.cn: 老舵跪了下来，把耳朵贴在甲板上。

sentences.en: 'I can *sense* a hollow space below,' he said, 'about the size of a map chest.'
We shifted three planks aside.
sentences.cn: 我们移开了三块木板。

sentences.en: There it was: a locked box with a fresh storm-lily pressed under the latch, still warm.
sentences.cn: 它就在那里：一个上面夹着一朵新鲜风暴百合的上锁盒子，百合花还温热着。

rate:2.en: The tide chart nailed to the mast showed numbers in two columns. Silverfang traced the figures with one finger. 'The *rate* at which this channel fills — twelve feet per hour — means we have exactly one window to reach the lower cave,' she said. Bell was already untying the rope ladder. We moved fast, and the cave gave up its map shard just in time.
rate:2.cnHint: 银牙通过计算潮水上涨的____，判断出进入洞穴的唯一时机。
rate:2.hook: The water was at our knees before we reached the ladder again.
rate:2.line: 'Match your *rate* to the tide, not to your fear,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: The tide chart nailed to the mast showed numbers in two columns.
sentences.cn: 钉在桅杆上的潮汐图表显示着两列数字。

sentences.cn: 银牙用一根手指追踪这些数字。

sentences.en: 'The *rate* at which this channel fills — twelve feet per hour — means we have exactly one window to reach the lower cave,' she said.
Bell was already untying the rope ladder.
sentences.cn: 小铃已经在解绳梯了。

sentences.en: We moved fast, and the cave gave up its map shard just in time.
sentences.cn: 我们快速行动，洞穴及时交出了它的地图碎片。

action:2.en: The storm had pushed us off course, and our map was useless. Bell found a glass bottle wedged between two rocks on the edge of the island. Inside was a single rolled note. It read: 'When clouds circle twice, *action* is the only answer — move toward the light, not away.' We looked up. The clouds were already circling.
action:2.cnHint: 小铃在礁石缝里发现了一个玻璃瓶，里面的字条告诉我们，面对风暴时____才是唯一的出路。
action:2.hook: The clouds had already circled once.
action:2.line: Old Helm said, 'In a storm like this, *action* beats waiting every time.'

sentences.en: The storm had pushed us off course, and our map was useless.
sentences.cn: 风暴把我们吹离了航线，我们的地图也没用了。

sentences.en: Bell found a glass bottle wedged between two rocks on the edge of the island.
sentences.cn: 小铃在岛屿边缘的两块岩石之间发现了一个玻璃瓶。

sentences.en: Inside was a single rolled note.
sentences.cn: 里面卷着一张纸条。

sentences.en: It read: 'When clouds circle twice, *action* is the only answer — move toward the light, not away.'
We looked up.
sentences.cn: 我们抬起头。

sentences.en: The clouds were already circling.
sentences.cn: 云已经在旋转了。

program:2.en: Tucked inside a cracked lantern near the storm wall, Bell discovered a folded sheet of paper — an old *program* from a sky festival, its edges burned. Someone had circled one act in red ink and written beneath it: 'Find the singer. She knows the next island.' Old Helm smoothed the paper carefully and smiled.
program:2.cnHint: 小铃在一盏破灯笼里找到了一张旧____，上面圈出的线索指向了一位神秘的歌者。
program:2.hook: We had no idea the singer was already watching us.
program:2.line: Bell whispered, 'This *program* is old, but the name circled on it is still alive.'

sentences.en: Tucked inside a cracked lantern near the storm wall, Bell discovered a folded sheet of paper — an old *program* from a sky festival, its edges burned.
Someone had circled one act in red ink and written beneath it: 'Find the singer.

sentences.en: Old Helm smoothed the paper carefully and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵小心地展平了纸张，笑了。

situation:2.en: A sealed tin box sat in the hollow of a storm-bent tree. Inside was a letter from a traveller who had passed this way before us. They described our exact *situation* — stranded, map torn, wind rising — and then listed three steps that had led them safely on. Old Helm read it aloud twice, slowly.
situation:2.cnHint: 一只铁盒里藏着一封信，信中描述的____与我们此刻的处境一模一样，还留下了脱困的方法。
situation:2.hook: The third step on the list made everyone go quiet.
situation:2.line: Old Helm read aloud: 'Whoever finds this shares our *situation* — so here is what worked for us.'

sentences.en: A sealed tin box sat in the hollow of a storm-bent tree.

sentences.en: Inside was a letter from a traveller who had passed this way before us.
sentences.cn: 盒子里是一封信，来自曾经经过这里的旅人。

sentences.en: They described our exact *situation* — stranded, map torn, wind rising — and then listed three steps that had led them safely on.
Old Helm read it aloud twice, slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵大声读了两遍，读得很慢。

order:2.en: Bell pulled a damp ledger from beneath a loose stone near the cliff edge. It was a cargo *order* — supplies bound for an island none of us had heard of. The name of that island was stamped in bright blue ink at the top. Old Helm pressed his finger to it and looked at me with wide eyes.
order:2.cnHint: 小铃在悬崖边的石头下发现了一份货物____，上面印着一个我们从未听说过的岛屿名称。
order:2.hook: That island name matched a gap on our torn map.
order:2.line: Silverfang leaned in and said, 'This *order* was meant for a place that should not exist.'

sentences.en: Bell pulled a damp ledger from beneath a loose stone near the cliff edge.
sentences.cn: 小铃从悬崖边一块松动的石头下拉出了一本潮湿的账本。

sentences.en: It was a cargo *order* — supplies bound for an island none of us had heard of.

sentences.cn: 那个岛的名字用亮蓝色的墨水印在了最上面。

sentences.cn: 老舵用手指按住它，然后用睁大的眼睛看着我。

event:2.en: Wedged behind a rusted weather vane, I found a notice board listing a single *event*: a gathering of island navigators, held once every hundred storms, at a place called the Still Eye. The date on the notice was tomorrow. Bell checked the wind direction and her face lit up.
event:2.cnHint: 我在一块布告板上发现了一条通知，上面记录着一个特别____，就在明天，就在风暴的中心。
event:2.hook: Tomorrow felt suddenly very close and very far.
event:2.line: Bell said, 'This *event* only happens once a century — and we are right on time.'

sentences.en: Wedged behind a rusted weather vane, I found a notice board listing a single *event*: a gathering of island navigators, held once every hundred storms, at a place called the Still Eye.
The date on the notice was tomorrow.

sentences.en: Bell checked the wind direction and her face lit up.
sentences.cn: 小铃检查了风向，她的脸亮了起来。

account:2.en: Inside a hollow navigation post near the storm wall, Bell found a hand-written *account* of a journey made thirty years ago. The writer described seeing a second sun rise from behind the lowest cloud and then vanish. Old Helm said nothing, but he folded the pages and tucked them close to his chest.
account:2.cnHint: 小铃找到了一份三十年前旅行者留下的____，里面记录了一件令人难以置信的奇异景象。
account:2.hook: Old Helm had the look of someone who had seen it too.
account:2.line: Old Helm murmured, 'This *account* matches something I once saw and never spoke about.'

sentences.en: Inside a hollow navigation post near the storm wall, Bell found a hand-written *account* of a journey made thirty years ago.
The writer described seeing a second sun rise from behind the lowest cloud and then vanish.
sentences.cn: 那位作者描述了他看到第二个太阳从最低的云层后升起，然后消失的情景。

sentences.en: Old Helm said nothing, but he folded the pages and tucked them close to his chest.
sentences.cn: 老舵什么都没说，但他把那些纸页折好，紧紧贴在胸口。

deal:2.en: The discovery was a carved wooden tablet propped against the storm barrier. It showed two figures shaking hands above a map, and the words beneath read: 'A great *deal* of sky still waits for those bold enough to cross the gap.' Someone had scratched an arrow beside the gap, pointing outward. I felt something lift in my chest.
deal:2.cnHint: 一块木牌上刻着两人握手的图案，文字提醒我们，仍有大____的天空等待着有勇气的旅人。
deal:2.hook: The arrow pointed to the exact gap in our broken map.
deal:2.line: Silverfang grinned and said, 'A great *deal* of sky is worth one small leap of faith.'

sentences.en: The discovery was a carved wooden tablet propped against the storm barrier.
sentences.cn: 这是一块靠着风暴屏障竖起来的雕刻木板。

sentences.en: It showed two figures shaking hands above a map, and the words beneath read: 'A great *deal* of sky still waits for those bold enough to cross the gap.'
Someone had scratched an arrow beside the gap, pointing outward.
sentences.cn: 有人在缝隙旁边划了一个箭头，指向外面。

sentences.en: I felt something lift in my chest.
sentences.cn: 我感到胸口有什么东西松了下来。

degree:2.en: Bell crouched over a brass dial half-buried in storm sand. It was a heading marker, and someone had scratched a note beside one *degree* on the dial — forty-seven — with the single word 'home' beneath it. Not our home. Someone else's. But it was a direction, and right now any direction felt like a gift.
degree:2.cnHint: 小铃在沙中发现了一个刻度盘，某个特定的____旁边刻着"家"这个词，为我们指明了方向。
degree:2.hook: Forty-seven degrees led straight into the heart of the next storm.
degree:2.line: Bell said quietly, 'One *degree* on this dial might be the difference between lost and found.'

sentences.en: Bell crouched over a brass dial half-buried in storm sand.
sentences.cn: 小铃蹲在半埋在风暴沙中的一个铜制刻度盘旁。

sentences.en: It was a heading marker, and someone had scratched a note beside one *degree* on the dial — forty-seven — with the single word 'home' beneath it.
Not our home.

sentences.cn: 是别人的。

sentences.en: But it was a direction, and right now any direction felt like a gift.
sentences.cn: 但它是一个方向，现在任何方向对我们来说都像是一份礼物。

mind:2.en: Deep in the storm sea, our ship tilted hard. Bell pressed one hand to her temple and closed her eyes. 'I need a moment,' she said softly. Her *mind* was the only map we had left — every current, every hidden reef, stored somewhere behind that calm face.
mind:2.cnHint: 小铃用她的____在脑海中搜寻每一条暗礁的位置。
mind:2.hook: Her eyes snapped open, and she pointed into the dark.
mind:2.line: 'Trust my *mind* — I know where the reef ends.'

sentences.en: Deep in the storm sea, our ship tilted hard.
sentences.cn: 在风暴海的深处，我们的船猛地倾斜了。

sentences.en: Bell pressed one hand to her temple and closed her eyes.
sentences.cn: 小铃一只手按在太阳穴上，闭上了眼睛。

sentences.en: 'I need a moment,' she said softly.
sentences.cn: "我需要喘口气，"她轻声说。

sentences.en: Her *mind* was the only map we had left — every current, every hidden reef, stored somewhere behind that calm face.

rise:2.en: We anchored beside a rock pillar as the storm eased. Old Helm pointed upward. A slow *rise* of warm air was lifting a torn sail like a flag, and wrapped inside it was a folded piece of bark — our next map fragment, drifting just above our reach.
rise:2.cnHint: 气流的____将一块树皮地图碎片托举到桅杆顶端。
rise:2.hook: The bark began to spin, and the stars behind it rearranged themselves.
rise:2.line: 'Watch that *rise* of air — something is caught inside it.'

sentences.cn: 老舵指向上方。

sentences.en: A slow *rise* of warm air was lifting a torn sail like a flag, and wrapped inside it was a folded piece of bark — our next map fragment, drifting just above our reach.

associate:2.en: At the storm's edge we found a drifting crate stamped with a silver fang. Bell said the mark made her *associate* it with the rival fleet at once. Inside lay a set of lens tools — too fine to leave behind, too strange to trust. We took them anyway.
associate:2.cnHint: 箱子上的标记让小铃立刻把它和竞争船队____在一起。
associate:2.hook: One of the lenses showed an island that appeared on no chart.
associate:2.line: 'I *associate* that stamp with Silverfang's eastern crew.'

sentences.en: We took them anyway.
sentences.cn: 我们还是把它带上了。

message:2.en: Tucked beneath the anchor chain we found a small tin box. Inside was a damp note — a *message* written in blue ink, addressed to no one by name but describing our ship's flag exactly. Someone out in the storm sea had been watching us for a long time.
message:2.cnHint: 锚链下藏着一个小铁盒，里面有一封写给我们的____。
message:2.hook: The ink was still wet, though the box had been sealed for days.
message:2.line: 'This *message* describes our flag down to the last stitch.'

development:2.en: Old Helm spread the new map fragment across the deck. 'Interesting *development*,' he said, tracing a dotted line that connected three islands we had already visited. They formed a triangle — and at its centre sat a location none of us had noticed before, hiding in plain sight.

development:2.hook: At the triangle's heart, a tiny mark pulsed like a slow heartbeat.
development:2.line: 'This is a surprising *development* — the islands form a shape.'

later:2.en: Bell sealed the message back in its tin and set it under her coat. 'We open it *later*,' she said firmly, 'once we are through the worst of the wind.' None of us argued. The storm was speaking louder than any note, and the mast was beginning to lean.

later:2.hook: The mast leaned further, and something heavy shifted below deck.
later:2.line: 'We read it *later* — right now, hold that rope tight.'

maintain:2.en: Halfway through the storm channel, the lantern above the helm began to flicker. Bell climbed the short ladder and cupped her hands around the flame. 'We must *maintain* this light,' she called down, 'or the rocks on the left side will not see us coming.' She was right, of course.

maintain:2.hook: The flame held, and something huge moved just beyond its edge.
maintain:2.line: '*Maintain* the light — we cannot afford darkness here.'

sentences.en: Halfway through the storm channel, the lantern above the helm began to flicker.

member:2.line: 'Every *member* of that old troupe is named here — and then there is you.'

Bell looked at me and smiled.
sentences.cn: 小铃看着我，笑了。

heart:2.en: At the storm's edge, where the clouds finally broke, we found a small island shaped like a crescent. Old Helm said the old charts called it the *heart* of the storm road — the still centre every lost ship had sailed toward without knowing. The air there was perfectly calm.
heart:2.cnHint: 在风暴边缘，我们找到一座月牙形小岛，老舵主说这里是整片风暴海域的____。
heart:2.hook: Carved into the island's only stone wall was a door with no handle.
heart:2.line: 'Old maps call this place the *heart* of the storm road — the calm at the centre.'

sentences.en: At the storm's edge, where the clouds finally broke, we found a small island shaped like a crescent.
sentences.cn: 在风暴的边缘，云层终于散开了，我们发现了一个新月形的小岛。

sentences.en: Old Helm said the old charts called it the *heart* of the storm road — the still centre every lost ship had sailed toward without knowing.
The air there was perfectly calm.
sentences.cn: 那里的空气完全静止不动。

worker:2.en: Deep in the storm-wracked island's lower decks, I found a carving on the wall — a single hand gripping a rope. Old Helm crouched beside me, brushing dust away. 'Every *worker* who crossed this sky left a mark,' he said quietly. 'We are not the first. We won't be the last.'
worker:2.cnHint: 在风暴岛的下层甲板，我们发现了一位____留下的印记。
worker:2.hook: Beneath the carving, a hidden door began to creak open.
worker:2.line: 'Every *worker* who crossed this sky left a mark.'

sentences.en: Deep in the storm-wracked island's lower decks, I found a carving on the wall — a single hand gripping a rope.
sentences.cn: 在风暴肆虐的岛屿的下层甲板深处，我发现了墙上的一个雕刻——一只手紧紧握着绳子。

sentences.en: Old Helm crouched beside me, brushing dust away.
sentences.cn: 老舵蹲在我身边，拂掉了灰尘。

sentences.en: 'Every *worker* who crossed this sky left a mark,' he said quietly.
'We are not the first.
sentences.cn: "我们不是第一个。

sentences.en: We won't be the last.'
sentences.cn: 也不会是最后一个。"

control:2.en: The storm wheel spun wildly. Bell grabbed the handles with both hands, feet planted wide, jaw tight. She showed me how to read the wind by feel, not by sight. 'You don't fight it,' she said. 'You *control* the sail, not the sky.' The island steadied beneath us.
control:2.cnHint: 小铃教我如何____风暴中失控的船帆。
control:2.hook: Then a second storm rose, larger and darker, on our right.
control:2.line: 'You *control* the sail, not the sky — never forget that.'

sentences.en: The storm wheel spun wildly.
sentences.cn: 风暴轮狂野地旋转。

sentences.en: Bell grabbed the handles with both hands, feet planted wide, jaw tight.
sentences.cn: 小铃双手紧握把手，两脚叉开站稳，下颌绷紧。

sentences.en: She showed me how to read the wind by feel, not by sight.

sentences.en: 'You *control* the sail, not the sky.'
The island steadied beneath us.

product:2.en: Old Helm unrolled a map fragment we had found in the storm wreckage. It was no ordinary paper — smooth, faintly glowing, clearly the *product* of some lost island craft we had never seen before. Bell traced the edge with one finger and said nothing for a long moment.
product:2.cnHint: 老舵展开了一张残骸中发现的地图碎片，那是某种失传技艺的____。
product:2.hook: The glow on the map began slowly moving toward its edge.
product:2.line: 'This is the *product* of a craft none of us have ever seen.'

sentences.en: Old Helm unrolled a map fragment we had found in the storm wreckage.
sentences.cn: 老舵展开了一张我们从风暴残骸中找到的地图碎片。

sentences.en: It was no ordinary paper — smooth, faintly glowing, clearly the *product* of some lost island craft we had never seen before.
Bell traced the edge with one finger and said nothing for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 小铃用一根手指沿着边缘描摹，长时间什么都没说。

practice:2.en: Every morning Bell stood at the prow in the howling wind and called out island names from memory. I asked why. 'Old *practice* of all navigators,' she said, not turning around. 'You name the places you hope to reach. The sky listens.' I started doing it too, quietly, just in case.
practice:2.cnHint: 小铃每天早晨遵循导航员的老____，大声说出她希望抵达的岛屿名字。
practice:2.hook: That morning, one of the names she spoke appeared on our map.
practice:2.line: 'Old *practice* of all navigators — you name the places you hope to reach.'

sentences.en: Every morning Bell stood at the prow in the howling wind and called out island names from memory.
sentences.cn: 每个清晨小铃都站在船首，在呼啸的风中大声喊出她记忆里的岛屿名字。

sentences.en: I asked why.
sentences.cn: 我问她为什么。

sentences.en: 'Old *practice* of all navigators,' she said, not turning around.
'You name the places you hope to reach.
sentences.cn: "你说出你希望到达的地方。

sentences.cn: 天空会听见。"

sentences.en: I started doing it too, quietly, just in case.
sentences.cn: 我也开始这样做，只是很轻很轻，以防万一。

environment:2.en: The storm region had its own *environment* — air thick with salt and a faint purple haze that made everything look older than it was. Old Helm said creatures lived here that nowhere else could support. I spotted something large moving below the clouds and felt very small.
environment:2.cnHint: 风暴海域有着独特的____，老舵说这里生活着别处找不到的生物。
environment:2.hook: The large shape below the clouds rose slowly toward our hull.
environment:2.line: 'This *environment* is like nothing the outer islands can offer us.'

sentences.en: The storm region had its own *environment* — air thick with salt and a faint purple haze that made everything look older than it was.
Old Helm said creatures lived here that nowhere else could support.
sentences.cn: 老舵说这里生活着其他地方无法存活的生物。

sentences.en: I spotted something large moving below the clouds and felt very small.
sentences.cn: 我看到什么东西庞大的东西在云层下移动，顿时感到自己渺小无比。

system:2.en: Silverfang's ship ran on a *system* of coloured ropes and pulleys that covered every wall of her bridge. Each colour meant something — speed, direction, alarm, anchor. She caught me staring. 'Took three years to build,' she said, almost warmly. 'Touch the wrong one and we all swim home.'
system:2.cnHint: 银牙向我展示她船上那套精密的绳索____。
system:2.hook: One rope had been cut cleanly, and no one knew when.
system:2.line: 'Took three years to build this *system* — do not touch the wrong rope.'

sentences.en: Silverfang's ship ran on a *system* of coloured ropes and pulleys that covered every wall of her bridge.
Each colour meant something — speed, direction, alarm, anchor.
sentences.cn: 每种颜色都有含义——速度、方向、警报、锚。

sentences.en: She caught me staring.
sentences.cn: 她察觉到我在盯着看。

sentences.en: 'Took three years to build,' she said, almost warmly.
sentences.cn: "花了三年才造好的，"她说，语气几乎是温暖的。

sentences.en: 'Touch the wrong one and we all swim home.'
sentences.cn: "碰错一根就得我们都游回家了。"

natural:2.en: Old Helm pointed to the way the storm clouds parted around one small island, leaving it in a circle of calm. '*Natural* shelter,' he said, spreading his hands like it was obvious. 'The island's shape guides the wind around itself.' We steered toward it, hoping the calm would hold long enough.
natural:2.cnHint: 老舵发现了一座小岛天然的____避风处。
natural:2.hook: As we drew close, lights appeared inside the island's dark cave mouth.
natural:2.line: '*Natural* shelter — the island itself guides the storm away.'

sentences.en: Old Helm pointed to the way the storm clouds parted around one small island, leaving it in a circle of calm. '*Natural* shelter,' he said, spreading his hands like it was obvious.
'The island's shape guides the wind around itself.'
sentences.cn: "岛屿的形状把风引导到自己周围。"

sentences.en: We steered toward it, hoping the calm would hold long enough.
sentences.cn: 我们朝它驶去，希望这份平静能坚持够久。

free:2.en: Silverfang cut the tangled rope that had caught in our anchor line without asking, then raised one hand before I could thank her. 'Debt goes both ways out here,' she said. 'Your anchor is *free*. Mine will need freeing someday.' She sailed off before Old Helm could say a word.
free:2.cnHint: 银牙帮我们解开了缠住锚链的绳索，让锚重新____了。
free:2.hook: But she left behind a small sealed note tied to the rail.
free:2.line: 'Your anchor is *free* — and someday mine will need the same.'

sentences.en: Silverfang cut the tangled rope that had caught in our anchor line without asking, then raised one hand before I could thank her.
sentences.cn: 银牙没有问一句就割断了缠在我们锚索上的乱绳，然后在我还没来得及道谢时抬起一只手。

sentences.en: 'Debt goes both ways out here,' she said.
sentences.cn: 她说，"在这儿，人情债是双向的。"

sentences.en: 'Your anchor is *free*.
Mine will need freeing someday.'
sentences.cn: 我的锚总有一天也会需要人来解救。

sentences.en: She sailed off before Old Helm could say a word.
sentences.cn: 她扬帆离开了，没给老舵说话的机会。

within:2.en: The storm had pushed us deep into the cloud layer, and Bell found a sealed bottle *within* the wreckage of an old signal tower. Inside was a folded chart — an island none of us had ever seen marked. Old Helm held it up to the starlight and smiled slowly, as if the sky itself had left us a note.
within:2.cnHint: 小铃在残破的信号塔废墟中发现了一个密封瓶，里面藏着一张从未见过的____地图。
within:2.hook: The chart showed a second bottle, hidden somewhere on the very island we stood on.
within:2.line: 'Everything we need is *within* this one small bottle,' Bell whispered.

sentences.en: The storm had pushed us deep into the cloud layer, and Bell found a sealed bottle *within* the wreckage of an old signal tower.
Inside was a folded chart — an island none of us had ever seen marked.
sentences.cn: 里面是一张折叠的海图——一个我们都没见过的岛屿被标了出来。

sentences.en: Old Helm held it up to the starlight and smiled slowly, as if the sky itself had left us a note.
sentences.cn: 老舵将它举向星光，缓缓一笑，仿佛天空本身给我们留下了一张纸条。

either:2.en: Two tunnels opened in the cliff face — one glowing amber, one cold blue. Old Helm studied both and shook his head. 'I do not trust *either* of these,' he said quietly. Bell pressed her ear to the amber wall and heard a faint hum, like a word trying to speak itself. We chose amber.
either:2.cnHint: 面对悬崖上两条颜色不同的通道，老舵说他____条都不信任，但小铃听到了奇怪的声音。
either:2.hook: Behind us, the blue tunnel sealed itself shut with a sound like a held breath.
either:2.line: 'I wouldn't take *either* path without listening first,' Bell said firmly.

sentences.en: Two tunnels opened in the cliff face — one glowing amber, one cold blue.
sentences.cn: 悬崖面上开着两条隧道——一条闪烁琥珀色，一条冰冷的蓝。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied both and shook his head.
sentences.cn: 老舵研究了两条，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: 'I do not trust *either* of these,' he said quietly.
Bell pressed her ear to the amber wall and heard a faint hum, like a word trying to speak itself.
sentences.cn: 小铃把耳朵贴在琥珀色的岩壁上，听到了一声细微的嗡鸣，就像某个词在试图说出自己。

sentences.en: We chose amber.
sentences.cn: 我们选了琥珀色的。

various:2.en: Scattered across the storm-washed deck were *various* objects left behind by earlier travellers — a cracked compass, three dried flowers, a list of words in faded ink. Old Helm gathered them carefully, one by one. Each item, he said, was a small story. Together, they might spell a name we needed.
various:2.cnHint: 暴风雨过后的甲板上散落着____各异的旅行者遗物，老舵一一收集，说它们合在一起也许能拼出一个名字。
various:2.hook: The last word on the faded list was the name of our ship.
various:2.line: '*Various* travellers left these clues — each one matters,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Scattered across the storm-washed deck were *various* objects left behind by earlier travellers — a cracked compass, three dried flowers, a list of words in faded ink.
Old Helm gathered them carefully, one by one.
sentences.cn: 老舵一个接一个地仔细收起它们。

sentences.en: Each item, he said, was a small story.
sentences.cn: 他说，每件物品都是一个小故事。

sentences.en: Together, they might spell a name we needed.
sentences.cn: 加在一起，它们也许能拼出一个我们需要的名字。

main:2.en: Bell spread the chart on the table and tapped the largest island at its centre. 'That is the *main* hub — every route passes through it.' The word written across it glowed faintly when she touched it, as if it had been waiting for exactly her finger. Old Helm nodded and quietly began packing.
main:2.cnHint: 小铃指着地图中央最大的岛屿说那是____枢纽，地图上的单词在她触碰时发出了微光。
main:2.hook: The word on the map rearranged its letters the moment Old Helm turned away.
main:2.line: 'The *main* island is where all lost routes come home,' Bell said softly.

sentences.en: Bell spread the chart on the table and tapped the largest island at its centre.
sentences.cn: 小铃在桌上铺开海图，轻轻敲了一下其中最大的中心岛屿。

sentences.en: 'That is the *main* hub — every route passes through it.'
The word written across it glowed faintly when she touched it, as if it had been waiting for exactly her finger.
sentences.cn: 那个词在她触碰到它时发出淡淡的光芒，仿佛在等待正好是她的这根手指。

sentences.en: Old Helm nodded and quietly began packing.
sentences.cn: 老舵点点头，默默开始收拾东西。

employee:2.en: Tucked inside a cracked lantern was a folded note. It read: 'To any *employee* of the Sky Chart Guild — the next word is hidden beneath the third flagstone.' Old Helm laughed at the word. We were no guild workers, but the flagstone was right there, and curiosity is its own kind of membership.
employee:2.cnHint: 破灯笼里藏着一张纸条，写给某个公会的____，提示下一个词就藏在第三块石板下面。
employee:2.hook: Under the flagstone lay not a word, but a key shaped like a question mark.
employee:2.line: 'Any *employee* of the Guild would know what this lantern means,' Old Helm read aloud.

sentences.en: Tucked inside a cracked lantern was a folded note.
sentences.cn: 一个裂开的灯笼里面折叠着一张纸条。

sentences.en: It read: 'To any *employee* of the Sky Chart Guild — the next word is hidden beneath the third flagstone.'
Old Helm laughed at the word.
sentences.cn: 老舵被这个词逗笑了。

sentences.en: We were no guild workers, but the flagstone was right there, and curiosity is its own kind of membership.
sentences.cn: 我们不是工会的工人，但那块旗石就在那里，而好奇心本身就是一种会员资格。

class:2.en: The recovered logbook sorted every island into a *class* — wild, settled, drifting, or dead. Our next destination was listed as drifting, which Bell said meant it moved slowly but never stopped. Silverfang crossed her arms. 'Then we do not aim at where it is,' she said. 'We aim at where it will be.'
class:2.cnHint: 找到的航海日志把每座岛屿分成不同的____，下一个目的地被列为"漂移型"，银牙说瞄准的应该是它将来的位置。
class:2.hook: The logbook's final page listed one island with no class at all — just a single question mark.
class:2.line: 'A drifting *class* island never waits for anyone,' Silverfang said with a sharp grin.

sentences.en: The recovered logbook sorted every island into a *class* — wild, settled, drifting, or dead.
Our next destination was listed as drifting, which Bell said meant it moved slowly but never stopped.
sentences.cn: 小铃说下一个目的地被列为漂流岛，意思是它移动得很慢但永远不会停下来。

sentences.en: 'Then we do not aim at where it is,' she said.

sentences.en: 'We aim at where it will be.'
sentences.cn: "我们瞄准它将要到达的地方。"

behavior:2.en: The small cloud-fox that had followed our ship for two days suddenly changed its *behavior* — it stopped circling and flew straight toward a gap in the storm wall. Bell grabbed her scope. Beyond the gap, just visible through the rain, was a shelf of pale rock we had no name for yet. The fox knew.
behavior:2.cnHint: 一直跟随船只的云狐突然改变了____，径直飞向暴风云的缺口，小铃用望远镜发现了一片未知的岩架。
behavior:2.hook: When Bell lowered her scope, the fox was gone — and a single feather lay on the chart.
behavior:2.line: 'Watch its *behavior* — animals always know before we do,' Bell said quietly.

sentences.en: The small cloud-fox that had followed our ship for two days suddenly changed its *behavior* — it stopped circling and flew straight toward a gap in the storm wall.
Bell grabbed her scope.
sentences.cn: 小铃抓起了她的望远镜。

sentences.en: Beyond the gap, just visible through the rain, was a shelf of pale rock we had no name for yet.
sentences.cn: 穿过风暴墙的缝隙，隐约可见雨中一块苍白的岩石架，我们还没给它起过名字。

sentences.en: The fox knew.
sentences.cn: 狐狸知道。

disease:2.en: The old keeper's log listed a *disease* that had swept through the island long ago — not one that harmed people, but one that made every written word fade to nothing within a day. The islanders had learned to carry their words in memory instead, and their spoken maps were said to be the most accurate in the sky.
disease:2.cnHint: 旧守护者的日志记载了一种曾席卷小岛的____，它让所有文字在一天内消失，岛民因此练就了靠记忆传递地图的本领。
disease:2.hook: The last line of the log had already begun to fade as I finished reading it.
disease:2.line: 'That *disease* taught them to trust memory more than ink,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: The old keeper's log listed a *disease* that had swept through the island long ago — not one that harmed people, but one that made every written word fade to nothing within a day.
The islanders had learned to carry their words in memory instead, and their spoken maps were said to be the most accurate in the sky.
sentences.cn: 岛上的人学会了用记忆力来保存他们的词语，他们的口头地图据说是天空中最精准的。

prove:2.en: A sealed bottle tumbled onto our deck from the storm clouds above. Inside was a folded note, its ink still dry. Bell unrolled it carefully and read aloud. The message was short: a set of star positions and a single question — could we reach the hidden reef before the next tide? Old Helm smiled. 'This will *prove* whether we belong in these waters.'

prove:2.hook: The tide clock on the mast had already begun to count down.
prove:2.line: 'This will *prove* whether we belong in these waters.'

sentences.en: 'This will *prove* whether we belong in these waters.'

maybe:0.en: Rain hammered the deck all morning, so the troupe gathered inside the old chart room. Maps covered every wall, their edges soft from sea air. degree:0.en: The chart room lantern swayed as the ship tilted. Bell knelt by a brass instrument on the floor, counting marks along its curved edge. member:0.en: The storm kept us all below deck for hours. Old Helm lit the centre lantern and looked around the room. 'Every *member* of this troupe has crossed rough water before,' he said, and his calm voice made the ceiling feel higher somehow. I was the newest one here, but in that warm light, surrounded by Bell and Silverfang, I felt the word include me too.
member:0.cnHint: 暴风雨中，老舵望着大家说，这支队伍的每一个____都经历过风浪，新来的叙述者第一次感到真正被接纳。
member:0.hook: Silverfang slid a spare chart across the table toward me.
member:0.line: 'Every *member* here has earned their place on this ship.'

sentences.en: The storm kept us all below deck for hours.
sentences.cn: 暴风雨让我们都在甲板下呆了好几个小时。

sentences.en: Old Helm lit the centre lantern and looked around the room.
sentences.cn: 老舵点燃了中央的灯笼，看向房间周围。

sentences.en: 'Every *member* of this troupe has crossed rough water before,' he said, and his calm voice made the ceiling feel higher somehow.
I was the newest one here, but in that warm light, surrounded by Bell and Silverfang, I felt the word include me too.
sentences.cn: 我是这里最新来的，但在那温暖的灯光下，被小铃和银牙围绕着，我感觉那个词也包括了我。
